senses.title: Skill in making things by hand
senses.definition: the trained ability to shape materials with tools, judged by what the hand produces
senses.definitionCN: 用工具加工材料、以手的成品为评判依据的受训能力
senses.example: She learned the craft of bookbinding from her aunt.
senses.exampleCN: 她跟着姑母学会了书籍装帧这门手艺。
senses.why: Old English cræft already joined strength with trained skill, so the word names ability before it names any object.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 cræft 已把力气与受训的技艺合在一起，因此这个词先指能力，后指物件。

senses.title: A trade built on that skill
senses.titleCN: 建立在手艺之上的行业
senses.definition: an occupation whose daily practice depends on trained handwork
senses.definitionCN: 日常作业依赖受训手工的行业
senses.example: The potter's craft has almost disappeared from this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 陶匠这门行业在这个山谷里几乎消失了。
senses.why: A skill held by a group becomes a recognized occupation, and the same noun names both.
senses.whyCN: 一群人所持有的技艺会成为被承认的行业，同一个名词便兼指两者。

senses.title: Handmade objects taken together
senses.definition: things made by hand, especially when displayed or sold as a group
senses.definitionCN: 手工制作的物件，尤指成批展示或出售时
senses.example: The fair fills three halls with local craft.
senses.exampleCN: 集市用三个展厅摆满了本地手工艺品。
senses.why: English often uses an uncountable noun for a class of goods, so the skill's products are named by the skill itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用不可数名词指一类货品，于是技艺的产物就用技艺本身来命名。

senses.title: Cunning instead of honest means
senses.definition: skill turned toward deceit, as when an aim is gained by craft rather than by fair means
senses.definitionCN: 把技艺转向欺瞒，如靠算计而非正当手段达到目的
senses.example: He won the seat by craft rather than by argument.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠手腕而非论辩赢得了这个席位。
senses.why: The old sense 'power' survives here as power over people, and skill in that domain reads as cunning.
senses.whyCN: 旧义「力量」在此留存为对人的支配力，而在这一领域里的技巧就被读作狡诈。

senses.title: A small boat
senses.definition: a small open boat or one with a light cover, usually worked by oars or a small engine
senses.definitionCN: 小型敞船或仅有轻质遮蔽的船，通常靠桨或小发动机行驶
senses.example: They rowed a wooden craft across the bay before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前他们划一条木船穿过海湾。
senses.why: The container sense grew from the idea of a shaped thing, and boats are the oldest objects called craft in this way.
senses.whyCN: 容器义由「被塑造之物」的观念生长出来，而船是最早这样被称为 craft 的物件。

senses.title: An aircraft or spacecraft
senses.definition: any vehicle designed to travel through air or space
senses.definitionCN: 任何设计为在空中或太空航行的载具
senses.example: The crew abandoned the burning craft seconds before impact.
senses.exampleCN: 机组在撞击前几秒弃离了起火的飞行器。
senses.why: A vessel sense needs no wheels or oars, so the word simply widened to vehicles that fly.
senses.whyCN: 航行器义并不要求轮子或桨，因此这个词顺理成章地扩展到会飞的载具。

senses.title: Skill in a field that is not manual
senses.definition: trained ability applied to writing, politics or teaching rather than to a material
senses.definitionCN: 用于写作、政治或教学而非用于材料的受训能力
senses.example: She practises the craft of the short story every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天上午练习短篇小说的写法。
senses.why: Once 'trained ability' is abstracted from the hand, any discipline with rules can be called a craft.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「受训能力」从手上抽离，任何有规矩可循的技艺领域都能被称作 craft。

senses.title: To make with deliberate skill
senses.titleCN: 以刻意的技艺制作（动词）
senses.definition: to shape or produce something with care, as a verb
senses.definitionCN: 作为动词，指用心思与技艺塑造或产出某物
senses.example: The team crafted a proposal that answered every objection.
senses.exampleCN: 团队精心拟出一份回应了每一条异议的提案。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: instead of the skill that a thing shows, it is the act of putting that skill in.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词反过来用：不再是物件显露的技艺，而是把技艺放进去的动作。

intro.en: Craft is one of the oldest native words in this batch: a Germanic noun that came to English with the sense of power and trained skill, then widened to a trade, a boat and an aircraft.
intro.cn: craft 是本批中最古老的本族词之一：一个日耳曼语名词带着「力量与受训技艺」之义进入英语，随后扩展到行业、小船与飞行器。

items.en: Cræft meant 'power, strength, skill, art'. The same noun covered a strong body and a trained hand, which is why the modern word still carries both an ability and a quality.
items.cn: cræft 意为「力量、气力、技艺、手艺」。同一个名词既涵盖强壮的身体也涵盖受训的手，因此现代词仍同时带着能力与品质两面。

items.en: The Old English form is generally traced to a Germanic noun reconstructed as *kraftiz 'power, force'. The reconstruction is standard at that level and makes no claim about an older source.
items.cn: 这个古英语形式一般追溯到重构为 *kraftiz「力量、气力」的日耳曼语名词。该重构在该层面属通说，且不对更早的来源作任何断言。

items.en: Middle English keeps the senses of skill and of a trade; the craft of a guild is a body of rules as much as a body of technique.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了技艺与行业两个义项；行会的 craft 既是一套技法，也是一套规矩。

items.en: The boat sense is recorded in the seventeenth century, when small vessels were called craft; the word for skill thereby becomes a word for a shaped thing that floats.
items.cn: 小船义在十七世纪有记录，当时小型船只被称作 craft；指技艺的词由此变成指一件成形漂浮之物的词。

items.en: Aircraft and spacecraft extend the vessel sense to vehicles that fly; the compound is formed in English and keeps the older noun inside it.
items.cn: aircraft 与 spacecraft 把航行器义扩展到会飞的载具；这些复合词在英语中构成，内部保留着这个更古老的名词。

items.en: What lies behind Germanic *kraftiz is uncertain; suggestions pointing to a root for 'power' remain reconstructions rather than demonstrated derivations.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *kraftiz 之后是什么，来源不确定；把它指向某个表「力量」的词根的说法仍属重构，而非已证实的派生。

note.en: The first group holds forms built on the same stem that are constantly mixed up with craft; the second holds words that overlap in meaning without sharing the history.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干构成、常与 craft 混用的形式；第二组是意思重叠但来历不同的词。

entries.definition: The adjective from craft, but the skill it names is used to deceive; a crafty plan is clever and dishonest.
entries.definitionCN: craft 的形容词形式，但它说的技艺用于欺瞒；指既机巧又不老实的计划。

entries.definition: The abstract noun judges how well something was made, whereas craft names the ability that made it.
entries.definitionCN: 这个抽象名词评判东西做得多好，而 craft 指做出它的能力。

entries.definition: Not a kind of skill: here craft means a vehicle, and air marks the medium.
entries.definitionCN: 并非一种技艺：此处 craft 指载具，air 标出所处介质。

entries.definition: Witch plus craft, naming a supposed magical practice; the second element keeps the old sense of a technique.
entries.definitionCN: witch 加 craft，指所谓的法术；第二个成分保留了「技法」的旧义。

entries.definition: Trained ability of any kind, mental or manual; craft adds the hand, the material and a standard of finish.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何受训能力，心智或手工皆可；craft 另带手工、材料与完成度标准。

entries.definition: A skilled occupation, viewed as a job with rules and a market; craft stresses the technique inside the job.
entries.definitionCN: 有技艺的行业，被视为有规矩与市场的职业；craft 更强调职业内部的技术。

entries.definition: Skill directed at expression and beauty; craft can serve art but does not require beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 指向表达与美的技艺；craft 可以为艺术服务，但并不要求美。

entries.definition: A single way of doing a step, countable and specific; craft is the whole trained ability behind many techniques.
entries.definitionCN: 把某一步做好的单一方法，可数而具体；craft 是支撑许多技法的整体受训能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One Germanic noun gave skill, trade, cunning, boat and aircraft: five readings of 'a shaped thing'.
normal.cn: 一个日耳曼名词给出了技艺、行业、算计、小船与飞行器：五种「被塑造之物」的读法。

normal.en: The family runs craft, craftsman, craftswoman, craftsmanship, crafty, handcraft, aircraft.
normal.cn: 同族词有 craft、craftsman、craftswoman、craftsmanship、crafty、handcraft、aircraft。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the skill sense: learn the craft, a master of the craft, the craft of writing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技艺义：学这门手艺、这门手艺的大师、写作的技艺。

normal.en: The boat sense survives in small craft warning, the maritime notice for fragile vessels.
normal.cn: 小船义仍活在海事警报的「小型船只警告」一语中，指小型船只。

normal.en: The verb is common in modern writing: craft a reply, craft a policy, carefully crafted.
normal.cn: 动词在现代写作中常见：精心拟一份答复、精心制定政策、精心打造的。

abstract.en: Picture a knife taking away everything that is not the boat.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刀把所有「不是船」的部分都削掉。

abstract.en: Picture a guild hall where the same word means the skill, the trade and the rules.
abstract.cn: 想象一座行会大厅，同一个词同时指技艺、行业与规矩。

abstract.en: Picture a hangar where the word for a rowing boat now holds a machine that flies.
abstract.cn: 想象一间机库，那个原指划艇的词如今装着一台会飞的机器。

examples.en: The frame is joined by hand, with the craft of a furniture maker trained in the old school.
examples.cn: 框架用手工接合，带着老派训练出来的家具匠手艺。

examples.en: Nobody teaches the craft of listening, though every negotiator needs it.
examples.cn: 没有人教倾听这门功夫，尽管每个谈判者都需要它。

examples.en: The little craft slipped between the rocks and reached the far shore.
examples.cn: 那条小船从礁石间穿过，抵达了远岸。

dict_mnemonic.text: craft 一身三任：手上的技艺、靠技艺吃饭的行当、被技艺塑成的东西；先记「手」，再延伸到行业与船。

root: 古英语 cræft「力量、技艺」，一般追溯到日耳曼语 *kraftiz「力量」；更早来源不确定。同族英语词有 crafty、craftsman，另有 aircraft、witchcraft 等复合形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses revolve around one act of shaping: the trained hand, the trade that lives on it, the objects it leaves, the cunning version of it, the boats and aircraft built by it, its use in non-manual fields, and finally the verb that puts it in.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个塑造动作：受训的手、靠它存续的行业、它留下的物件、它转为算计的版本、由它造出的船与飞行器、它在非手工领域的运用，最后是把技艺放进去的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade removing what is not yet the thing, until the shape inside the wood appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把刀削去还不是那件东西的部分，直到木头里的形状显露出来。

branches.en: ABILITY BECOMES OCCUPATION: a skill held by a person is held by a group, and a group that lives by it becomes a trade.
branches.cn: 能力成为行业：个人持有的技艺被一群人持有，靠它吃饭的一群人就成为行业。

branches.en: FROM RESULT BACK TO ACT: the objects are craft, and the making of them is also to craft.
branches.cn: 从结果回到动作：物件是 craft，制作这些物件的动作也是 craft。

branches.en: POWER OVER PEOPLE: the old sense of force survives as skill used against others, which reads as cunning.
branches.cn: 对人的支配：旧义「力量」留存为对他人使用的技巧，读作狡诈。

branches.en: A SHAPED THING THAT CARRIES: first a hull that floats, then any vehicle that flies.
branches.cn: 能载人的成形之物：先是一具漂浮的船体，再是任何会飞的载具。

branches.en: THE HAND ABSTRACTED: once skill is separable from material, writing and politics have crafts too.
branches.cn: 抽离双手：一旦技艺可与材料分离，写作与政治也就各有其 craft。

intro.en: Craft works both as a free noun and as a combining element, and the compounds below show how far the shaping idea travels.
intro.cn: craft 既可作独立名词，也可作构词成分，下面的复合词显示「塑造」这一观念能走多远。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin source: craft and its compounds are native Germanic formations, and the borrowed-looking members of the family are independent words that merely share the shape.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁来源：craft 及其复合词都是本族日耳曼语形式，家族中看似借词的那些成员只是外形相同，另有独立来历。

items.structure: craft (Old English noun and verb stem)
items.example: The bare stem serves as both noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干光用即可兼作名词与动词。

items.example: Compounds split between the technique and the vessel sense.
items.exampleCN: 复合词分别落在技术义与载具义上。

items.example: The suffix turns skill into a personality trait.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把技艺变成一种性格特征。

items.example: The compound personifies the skill.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把技艺人格化。

items.example: Only the sex marker differs from craftsman.
items.exampleCN: 与 craftsman 相比只换了性别标记。

items.meaning: the maker's standing or the work's quality
items.example: The long form is used for judging work.
items.exampleCN: 这个长形式用于评判做工。

items.example: Here craft is the product, not the ability.
items.exampleCN: 此处 craft 指产物而非能力。

items.example: The vessel sense needs only a medium.
items.exampleCN: 载具义只需补上一种介质。

items.example: The pattern repeats for the medium beyond the sky.
items.exampleCN: 同一模式在天空之外的介质上重复。

items.example: The oldest sense of technique survives in a superstitious label.
items.exampleCN: 最古老的技法义留存在一个迷信标签里。

definition_zh: 工匠；手艺人；以手工小批量制作并留名于作品的匠人
definition_en: a skilled worker who makes things by hand, usually in small quantities
core_image: 一人一炉一案，面包在掌下成形，炉门上还留着手抹的泥
scene: 清晨的作坊里，面包师把面团从木盆取出，用手掌压出气孔，再送进砖炉。An artisan marks each loaf with a small slash so buyers know whose hands made it.
sceneCN: 这里 artisan 指「以手工小批量制作、作品带个人印记的匠人」（第 6 个义项：以个人风格为标志的制作者）；句意为这位匠人在每条面包上划一道小口作记号，好让买者知道出自谁手。

pos.zh: 工匠；手艺人（可数；亦作定语，如「匠人面包」这一说法）

derivatives.zh: artisan + -al（形容词后缀）→ 手工制作的（语义偏移：从人转向产品属性）
artisan + -ship（状态）→ 匠人身份与技艺
拉丁 ars（技艺）→ 艺术（同根不同线，经古法语进入英语）
art + -ist（从事者）→ 艺术家（同根，但走的是 art 而非 artisan 这条线）
arte（技艺）+ factum（做成之物）→ 人工制品
art + -fice（facere，做）→ 巧计；人工技巧

senses.title: Skilled worker who makes by hand
senses.titleCN: 以手工制作的熟练工人
senses.definition: a person whose trade is shaping material with trained hands and tools
senses.definitionCN: 以受训的双手与工具加工材料为职业的人
senses.example: The bench was made by a local artisan from oak felled on the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 这条长凳由本地匠人用庄园里砍下的橡木制成。
senses.why: The word reaches English from Latin ars 'skill' through Italian and French, and it names the person who holds the skill rather than the skill.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经意大利语与法语从拉丁 ars「技艺」进入英语，指持有技艺的人，而不是技艺本身。

senses.title: Small-scale independent producer
senses.definition: a maker who works in a small workshop rather than a factory
senses.definitionCN: 在小作坊而非工厂里生产的制作者
senses.example: Artisans in the old quarter still sell directly from their workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区的匠人至今仍在作坊门口直接售卖。
senses.why: A hand worker cannot scale like a plant, so the word carries a built-in contrast with industry.
senses.whyCN: 靠手的人无法像工厂那样扩产，因此这个词自带与工业相对的含义。

senses.title: Maker of one traditional product
senses.titleCN: 某一种传统产品的制作者
senses.definition: a maker of a particular regional good such as cheese, bread, tile or lacquer ware
senses.definitionCN: 制作某一地方性产品的人，如奶酪、面包、屋瓦或漆器
senses.example: The village artisans still fire roof tiles in a wood kiln.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的匠人仍用柴窑烧制屋瓦。
senses.why: Long practice in one product turns a general hand worker into the named maker of that product.
senses.whyCN: 长期只做一种产品，会让一般的手工者变成该产品的具名制作者。

senses.title: Guild master in a medieval town
senses.titleCN: 中世纪城镇中的行会匠师
senses.definition: in medieval towns, a master of a trade organized under a guild
senses.definitionCN: 在中世纪城镇里，隶属于行会的行业师傅
senses.example: Only artisans of the guild could sell silver within the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 只有行会中的匠人才能在城墙内出售银器。
senses.why: Guilds turned a personal skill into a licensed status, and artisan was the word for that status.
senses.whyCN: 行会把个人技艺变成受许可的身份，artisan 正是指这一身份的词。

senses.title: Worker who owns the tools
senses.definition: in economic writing, a producer who owns the means of production instead of selling only labour
senses.definitionCN: 在经济文献中，拥有生产资料而非仅出卖劳动力的生产者
senses.example: The study compares artisans who own their looms with workers who rent them.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究比较了自有织机的匠人与租用织机的工人。
senses.why: Ownership follows from small-scale work: the person who makes the whole thing usually owns the bench.
senses.whyCN: 所有权由小规模作业而来：做完整件东西的人通常拥有那张工作台。

senses.title: Maker whose work carries a name
senses.titleCN: 作品带个人署名的制作者
senses.definition: a maker valued because individual pieces can be traced to one pair of hands
senses.definitionCN: 因单件作品可追溯到某一双手而受重视的制作者
senses.example: Collectors now pay more for pieces by named artisans than for factory sets.
senses.exampleCN: 藏家如今为有名有姓的匠人之作付的钱，比工厂成套品更多。
senses.why: Where output is not uniform, the maker becomes a brand, and the word acquires a market meaning.
senses.whyCN: 当产出并不均一时，制作者就成了品牌，这个词也随之带上市场含义。

senses.title: Deliberate maker outside manual work
senses.titleCN: 非手工领域的刻意制作者
senses.definition: a person who builds something carefully, said figuratively of writers, cooks or programmers
senses.definitionCN: 精心构建某物的人，可喻指写作者、厨师或程序员
senses.example: He calls himself an artisan of small, exact sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称是一个做短小而精确句子的人。
senses.why: If the essence is care plus a signature, the material can be words or code as easily as clay.
senses.whyCN: 若核心是用心加署名，那么材料换成文字或代码，与换成黏土并无不同。

senses.title: Attributive label for handmade goods
senses.titleCN: 标示手工制品的定语用法
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark a product as hand-made and small-batch
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标示产品为手工、小批量制作
senses.example: Artisan bread costs more because it is shaped and timed by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 手工面包更贵，因为它的成形与发酵都靠人手掌控。
senses.why: A noun that names a maker can stand before another noun and act as a certificate of origin.
senses.whyCN: 一个指制作者的名词可以放在另一名词前，充当产地与工艺的证明。

intro.en: Artisan is a Latin word that travelled through Italian and French before reaching English, and it keeps the workshop in view where artist keeps the studio.
intro.cn: artisan 是一个经意大利语与法语辗转进入英语的拉丁词；它眼里是作坊，而 artist 眼里是画室。

items.en: Ars, genitive artis, meant 'skill, craft, art'. It is generally connected with a Latin root for 'fitting together', reconstructed as *ar-, but that root is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: ars（属格 artis）意为「技艺、手艺、艺术」。它一般与一个表「接合」的拉丁词根相联系，重构为 *ar-，但该词根是重构形式，并非有记录的形式。

items.en: Artitus 'skilled, trained in an art' is the adjective built on ars that supplies the medieval stem of the word.
items.cn: artitus「有技艺的、受过训练的」是建于 ars 之上的形容词，提供了这个词的中世纪词干。

items.en: Spoken Latin formed *artitianus 'one who works at a craft'; the suffix -ianus marks a person belonging to or practising something.
items.cn: 口语拉丁构成 *artitianus「从事某门手艺的人」；后缀 -ianus 标出属于或从事某事的人。

items.en: Italian artigiano names a craftsman or tradesman and is the immediate source of the French form.
items.cn: 意大利语 artigiano 指工匠或手艺人，是法语形式的直接来源。

items.en: French artisan entered English in the sixteenth century, bringing with it the small workshop and the guild rather than the fine-art studio.
items.cn: 法语 artisan 于十六世纪进入英语，带来的是小作坊与行会，而不是美术画室。

items.en: English keeps the handwork sense and later adds the marketing sense of small-batch goods; the shared Latin root with art and artist is real, but the words arrived by different routes.
items.cn: 英语保留了手工义，后来又添上小批量货品的市场义；它与 art、artist 共享拉丁词根，但三者是经不同路径进入英语的。

note.en: The first group holds near-identical shapes, including one famous false friend; the second holds true synonyms with different emphases.
note.cn: 第一组是外形极近的词，其中一个是有名的假朋友；第二组是侧重点不同的真同义词。

entries.definition: Nothing to do with skill: it describes a well whose water rises under its own pressure, from the old province name Artois.
entries.definitionCN: 与技艺无关：指水靠自身压力上升的自流井，来自旧地名阿图瓦。

entries.definition: A maker of art, formed on art rather than on artisan; the two words share ars but came by different routes.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术创作者，由 art 而非 artisan 构成；两词共享 ars，但路径不同。

entries.definition: The adjective from artisan, now used mostly on goods and methods: artisanal cheese, artisanal mining.
entries.definitionCN: artisan 的形容词形式，如今多用于货品与方法：手工奶酪、手工采矿。

entries.definition: Art plus a form of facere 'to make'; it means a clever trick rather than honest handwork.
entries.definitionCN: art 加 facere「做」的某种形式；指巧计，而非诚实的手工。

entries.definition: The English-born equivalent; it stresses trained skill, while artisan stresses the small workshop and the trade status.
entries.definitionCN: 本族语中的对应词，强调受训技艺，而 artisan 强调小作坊与行会身份。

entries.definition: Anyone who makes something, including machines and companies; artisan implies a person and a hand.
entries.definitionCN: 任何制作者，包括机器与公司；artisan 隐含「人」与「手」。

entries.definition: A skilled worker who also sells, often at a shop or on a round; artisan usually makes rather than serves customers.
entries.definitionCN: 既制作也售卖、常守店面或走街的熟练者；artisan 通常只做不服务于顾客。

entries.definition: A worker in metal by name; artisan is the general term that covers clay, wood, cloth and food as well.
entries.definitionCN: 名字即指金属加工者；artisan 是涵盖陶、木、布、食的通称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ars 'skill' + -anus 'person concerned with': the one concerned with a skill.
normal.cn: ars「技艺」+ -anus「与…相关的人」：与某门技艺相关的那个人。

normal.en: The family runs artisan, artisanal, artisanship, and on the other line art, artist, artistic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 artisan、artisanal、artisanship，另一条线是 art、artist、artistic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark small-batch goods: artisan bread, artisan cheese, artisan goods.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出小批量货品：手工面包、手工奶酪、手工艺品。

normal.en: The workshop, not the studio, separates artisan from artist.
normal.cn: 分开 artisan 与 artist 的，是作坊而不是画室。

normal.en: The false friend artesian describes water under pressure, and it comes from a place name, not from a skill.
normal.cn: 假朋友 artesian 讲的是受压的水，来自地名，与技艺无关。

abstract.en: Picture a single pair of hands in a shop so small that the door is the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一间小到门口就是柜台、只有一双手在干的作坊。

abstract.en: Picture a loaf with a slash on top, the maker's name written in one stroke.
abstract.cn: 想象一条顶上划了一刀的面包，那一刀就是制作者的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a guild seal on a silver cup, turning skill into a legal right to sell.
abstract.cn: 想象银杯上的行会印记，把技艺变成售卖的合法权利。

examples.en: A retired engineer and a village artisan rebuilt the clock tower by hand.
examples.cn: 一位退休工程师和一位村里匠人用手工重修了钟楼。

examples.en: The shop sells only what its own artisans can finish in a week.
examples.cn: 这家店只卖自家匠人一周内能完成的东西。

examples.en: Tourism has turned cheese making from a farm task into a craft with named artisans.
examples.cn: 旅游业把做奶酪从农活变成了有具名匠人的手艺。

dict_mnemonic.text: art（技艺）+ isan（人）＝ 靠一门技艺吃饭的人；记「一双手、一间小作坊、一个名字」。

root: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺、艺术」+ 晚期拉丁 -ianus（从事某业的人）→ 意大利 artigiano → 法语 artisan；ars 更早来源一般重构为 *ar-「接合」，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a pair of hands to a market label: the hand worker, the small shop, the single product, the guild master, the owner of tools, the signed piece, the figurative maker, and the adjective on a loaf.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一双匠人的手出发走到一个市场标签：手工者、小作坊、单一产品、行会师傅、工具所有者、署名作品、比喻中的制作者，以及写在面包上的定语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pair of hands, one bench, one product, and a mark that says who made it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手、一张工作台、一种产品，以及一个标明出自谁手的记号。

branches.en: FROM HAND TO SPECIALITY: general hand skill narrows into the named maker of one traditional good.
branches.cn: 从手到专精：一般的手工技艺收窄为某一传统产品的具名制作者。

branches.en: SMALL SCALE AS A LABEL: the workshop facts become a word placed on goods to certify origin.
branches.cn: 小规模成为标签：作坊里的事实变成一个放在货品上、用来证明来历的词。

branches.en: STATUS AND OWNERSHIP: the guild licenses the trade, and the small producer owns the bench.
branches.cn: 身份与所有权：行会给行业发许可，小生产者拥有那张工作台。

branches.en: SIGNATURE VALUE: when pieces differ, a name on the piece becomes the reason to pay more.
branches.cn: 署名价值：当每件作品并不相同时，作品上的名字就成了多付钱的理由。

branches.en: MATERIAL BECOMES OPTIONAL: if care and signature define the word, words and code qualify as much as clay.
branches.cn: 材料成为可选：若核心是用心与署名，文字与代码和黏土一样够格。

intro.en: Artisan is built from a Latin noun of skill plus a Latin person suffix, and both parts still build English words on their own.
intro.cn: artisan 由一个表技艺的拉丁名词加一个拉丁人称后缀构成，两部分至今都能独立构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars supplies art, artist, artistic, artifice and inert through related forms; the person suffix -ianus supplies artisan, and the same pattern gives Italian artigiano and French artisan.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars 经由相关形式给出 art、artist、artistic、artifice 等词；人称后缀 -ianus 给出 artisan，同一模式也给出意大利语 artigiano 与法语 artisan。

items.example: The noun is the head of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的源头。

items.example: The adjective supplies the medieval stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供了中世纪词干。

items.meaning: one who works at a craft
items.example: The spoken form is reconstructed from its descendants.
items.exampleCN: 这个口语形式是由其后续语言重构出来的。

items.structure: art (English noun from Latin ars through Old French)
items.example: The short noun keeps only the aesthetic branch.
items.exampleCN: 这个短名词只保留了审美那一支。

items.example: The studio word, not the workshop word.
items.exampleCN: 这是画室的词，不是作坊的词。

items.example: The suffix moves the word from person to product.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词从人移到产品。

items.example: The suffix abstracts the person into a condition.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把人抽象成一种状态。

items.example: The compound joins skill with making.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把技艺与制作连在一起。

items.example: The same skill is here turned toward deception.
items.exampleCN: 同样的技艺在此转向欺瞒。

definition_zh: 贸易；交易；行业；（手）艺；行业中人；（球员）交换；交换；信风
definition_en: the buying and selling of goods, the business that does it, a skilled occupation, or an exchange of one thing for another
core_image: 两只手在柜台两侧各推出一件东西，谁也没有空手收回
scene: 集市收摊前，鱼贩把最后两筐鱼换给布商，换回三匹粗布。She learned to trade fish for cloth before she could write her own name.
sceneCN: 这里 trade 指「以货易货式的交换」（第 3 个义项：两方各以所有换所需）；句意为她还没会写自己的名字，就先学会了拿鱼换布。

pos.zh: 贸易；交易；行业；同行中人；（职业）手艺
从事贸易；交换；做买卖

derivatives.zh: trade + -er（从事者）→ 商人；交易者
trade + -ing（动名词）→ 交易活动；交易的
trade + -able（可…的）→ 可交易的
trade + -s + man → 店主；送货商（语义偏移：从行业转指上门服务者）
trade + off → 取舍（语义偏移：从交换转为代价权衡）
trade + mark → 商标（语义偏移：行业标记）

senses.title: Buying and selling of goods
senses.definition: the activity of buying and selling goods and services, especially between places
senses.definitionCN: 买卖货物与服务的活动，尤指发生在不同地方之间
senses.example: Trade between the two ports doubled in a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 两个港口之间的贸易十年间翻了一倍。
senses.why: The word began as a track or course and only in the sixteenth century shifted to the course goods take when sold.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指路径或行程，到十六世纪才转为货物被售出时所走的路线。

senses.title: A particular branch of business
senses.definition: one line of business, spoken of as a field with its own customs
senses.definitionCN: 某一业务门类，被视为有其自身规矩的领域
senses.example: She has worked in the book trade for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她在图书行业干了三十年。
senses.why: A course of dealing becomes a named field once enough people make it their living.
senses.whyCN: 当足够多的人以此为生，一条交易路径就变成一个有名目的领域。

senses.title: An exchange of one thing for another
senses.definition: the act of giving one thing and receiving another in return, with or without money
senses.definitionCN: 给出某物并换回另一物的行为，可含钱也可不含钱
senses.example: The two villages trade fish for cloth every Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 两个村子每逢周六拿鱼换布。
senses.why: Every sale is an exchange, so the general sense survives underneath the commercial one.
senses.whyCN: 每次买卖都是交换，因此一般义一直藏在商业义之下。

senses.title: A skilled occupation
senses.definition: a job that requires trained manual skill, learned by apprenticeship
senses.definitionCN: 需要受训手工技能、靠学徒制习得的职业
senses.example: He learned a trade at sixteen and never left it.
senses.exampleCN: 他十六岁学了一门手艺，此后就没离开过。
senses.why: A trade was a course of life before it was a course of goods; the two senses share the idea of a fixed path.
senses.whyCN: trade 在被用于货物流通之前先指一条人生路径；两个义项共享「固定路径」之意。

senses.title: The people in a business
senses.definition: the body of people engaged in a particular business, as in the trade will resist the rule
senses.definitionCN: 从事某一行业的整体人群，如「业内会抵制这条规定」
senses.example: The trade welcomed the new safety standard.
senses.exampleCN: 业内欢迎这项新的安全标准。
senses.why: A field metonymically stands for its members, a common shift from branch to people.
senses.whyCN: 领域以转喻方式代表其成员，这是从「行业」到「人」的常见转移。

senses.title: A swap between teams or players
senses.titleCN: 球队或球员之间的交换
senses.definition: an exchange of players between clubs, or of picks and contracts
senses.definitionCN: 俱乐部之间的球员交换，或选秀权与合同的交换
senses.example: The trade sent two young players to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易把两名年轻球员送去了海岸那边的球队。
senses.why: Sports borrowed the plain exchange sense and made it a countable event.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了普通的交换义，并把它变成可数的具体事件。

senses.title: To buy and sell as a business
senses.definition: to carry on commerce, especially across distance or borders
senses.definitionCN: 从事商业，尤指跨距离或跨境进行
senses.example: The company trades in timber and paper.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司做木材与纸张生意。
senses.why: The verb takes the commercial noun and turns it into repeated activity.
senses.whyCN: 动词把商业名词接过来，变成反复进行的活动。

senses.title: To exchange or swap
senses.definition: to give something and receive something else in return
senses.definitionCN: 给出某物并换回另一物
senses.example: They traded seats so the child could sit by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他们换了座位，好让孩子靠窗坐。
senses.why: The exchange sense is the oldest surviving one and needs no money at all.
senses.whyCN: 交换义是留存下来的最古老义项，完全不需要钱。

senses.title: A steady wind of the tropics
senses.definition: a wind that blows steadily in one direction in the tropics, used by sailing ships
senses.definitionCN: 热带地区持续吹向同一方向、供帆船利用的风
senses.example: Sailing ships waited for the trade winds before crossing the Atlantic.
senses.exampleCN: 帆船等信风起了才横渡大西洋。
senses.why: A route at sea came to be named for the winds that made it reliable, and the word for a course is again at work.
senses.whyCN: 海上的一条航路终以使它可靠的风命名，那个表「路径」的词又一次在起作用。

intro.en: Trade is not a Latin word at all: it came from a Germanic noun for a track, and the modern commercial sense is a late medieval development.
intro.cn: trade 根本不是拉丁词：它来自一个表「足迹、路径」的日耳曼名词，现代的商业义是中古晚期才发展出来的。

items.en: Trade meant 'track, course, path'. It reached English in the fourteenth century from the Low German spoken by merchants of the North Sea trade.
items.cn: trade 意为「足迹、行程、路径」。它在十四世纪由北海贸易的商人所说的低地德语进入英语。

items.en: The Low German noun is related to Old Saxon trada 'spoor, track' and to the English verb tread; all go back to the same Germanic idea of treading a path.
items.cn: 这个低地德语名词与古撒克逊语 trada「足迹、踪迹」以及英语动词 tread 同源，都回到日耳曼语「踩出一条路」的观念。

items.en: In Middle English trade still means a course or a way of life, as in the trade of a smith: the path a worker follows daily.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，trade 仍指一条路径或一种生活方式，如铁匠的 trade：工人每天走的那条路。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word is used for the buying and selling of goods; the path becomes the route goods travel between buyer and seller.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词已用于货物的买卖；路径变成了货物在买卖双方之间所走的路线。

items.en: Trade winds are named in the seventeenth century, because they made the sailing routes of the Atlantic predictable.
items.cn: 信风在十七世纪得名，因为它们让大西洋的帆船航线变得可预测。

items.en: Modern English separates the countable branch sense and the team-swap sense from the uncountable commerce sense, all from the same original path.
items.cn: 现代英语把可数的行业义、球队交换义与不可数的贸易义分开，但它们都出自最初那条「路径」。

note.en: The first group shares the stem and is easily mixed up; the second holds words for exchange and for occupation that trade overlaps with.
note.cn: 第一组共享词干，容易混淆；第二组是 trade 在交换义与职业义上重叠的词。

entries.definition: To walk or press with the foot; it is the verb whose noun became trade, and it keeps the physical sense of treading a path.
entries.definitionCN: 用脚踩踏；正是其名词演变为 trade 的那个动词，保留了踩出路径的本义。

entries.definition: A shopkeeper or skilled worker who visits customers; it names a person where trade names an activity or a field.
entries.definitionCN: 守店或上门服务的店主、技工；trade 指活动或领域，这个词指人。

entries.definition: A balance between two things you cannot both have; nothing is literally bought or sold.
entries.definitionCN: 两件不能兼得之事间的权衡；并无真正的买卖。

entries.definition: A registered sign of a business, formed as trade plus mark; it is not a transaction.
entries.definitionCN: 企业注册的标志，由 trade 加 mark 构成；并非一笔交易。

entries.definition: The formal word for buying and selling on a large scale, especially between regions; it lacks the exchange and occupation senses.
entries.definitionCN: 正式场合指大规模买卖，尤指区域之间；不含交换义与职业义。

entries.definition: Any commercial activity or firm, including services; trade usually implies goods moving between hands or places.
entries.definitionCN: 任何商业活动或企业，含服务业；trade 通常意味货物在人或地点之间流转。

entries.definition: Trade by goods only, with no coin passing; it is one narrow kind of trade.
entries.definitionCN: 只以货物交换、不经钱币；它是 trade 的一个窄类。

entries.definition: A person's job of any kind; trade as occupation adds the idea of trained manual skill.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何职业；trade 作职业义时另带受训手工技能之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One Germanic word for a track gave trade, trader, trading and the trade winds.
normal.cn: 一个表「路径」的日耳曼词给出了 trade、trader、trading 与信风。

normal.en: The family runs trade, trader, trading, tradable, tradesman, trade-off, trademark.
normal.cn: 同族词有 trade、trader、trading、tradable、tradesman、trade-off、trademark。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: foreign trade, the book trade, learn a trade, trade places.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：对外贸易、图书行业、学一门手艺、互换位置。

normal.en: Tread is the verb behind the noun: a path is what feet make.
normal.cn: tread 是这个名词背后的动词：路径是脚踩出来的。

normal.en: The winds carry the oldest sense: trade winds were named for the sailing routes they made reliable.
normal.cn: 风带着最古老的义项：信风因其使帆船航线可靠而得名。

abstract.en: Picture a path worn into grass between two villages, then paved, then crowded with carts of goods.
abstract.cn: 想象两村之间被踩出路痕的青草小径，先被铺平，再挤满载货的车。

abstract.en: Picture a seat exchanged on a train, the smallest possible trade.
abstract.cn: 想象列车上换一个座位，这是最小规模的一次 trade。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop door with a sign that names a skill instead of a product.
abstract.cn: 想象作坊门口挂着一块牌子，写的是一门手艺，而非一件产品。

examples.en: The island trades salt for grain with the mainland.
examples.cn: 这座岛用盐与大陆换谷物。

examples.en: He was apprenticed at fourteen and has followed the trade ever since.
examples.cn: 他十四岁当学徒，此后一直干这门手艺。

examples.en: Both clubs agreed to the trade before the deadline.
examples.cn: 两家俱乐部在截止前同意了这笔球员交换。

dict_mnemonic.text: trade＝被踩出来的路：人走出的路成了行业，货走的路成了贸易，风走的路成了信风。

root: 中古低地德语 trade「足迹、路径」，与古撒克逊语 trada「踪迹」及英语 tread 同源，属日耳曼语；十六世纪转指货物买卖。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow a single path: a track becomes a way of life, a way of life becomes an occupation, an occupation becomes an exchange, and an exchange becomes a field, a swap and finally a wind that keeps the route open.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一条路径展开：路痕成为一种生计，生计成为职业，职业成为交换，交换成为行业、成为一次具体的交换，最后成为让航线不断的风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a track worn between two places, along which things and people keep moving both ways.
core.cn: 核心意象：两地之间踩出的一条路痕，东西与人沿着它来回不断。

branches.en: ACTIVITY AND VERB: commerce as a mass activity, then the same activity as something a firm does daily.
branches.cn: 活动与动词：作为整体活动的贸易，再作为企业每天去做的事情。

branches.en: FIELD AND ITS PEOPLE: one line of business, then the people who collectively are that line.
branches.cn: 行业与其人：一条业务门类，然后是构成这条门类的那群人。

branches.en: THE PLAIN SWAP: goods for goods, players for players, seats for seats.
branches.cn: 纯粹的交换：货换货、球员换球员、座位换座位。

branches.en: A COURSE OF LIFE: the same path word names the occupation a person follows for decades.
branches.cn: 人生的路径：同一个「路径」词指一个人走上几十年的职业。

branches.en: A ROUTE MADE RELIABLE: the wind is named for the sea road it kept open.
branches.cn: 被风固定的航线：风因它所维持的海上道路而得名。

intro.en: Trade is a free noun and verb that also combines freely, and the compounds below show both the goods sense and the occupation sense at work.
intro.cn: trade 是能自由使用的名词与动词，也能自由复合，下面的词显示货品义与职业义如何各自运作。

latinIntro.en: Trade has no Latin ancestor: the stem is Germanic, related to tread, and the commercial meaning grew inside English. Only the compounds built with borrowed elements, such as trademark, contain Latin-derived parts.
latinIntro.cn: trade 没有拉丁语祖先：词干属日耳曼语，与 tread 同源，商业义是在英语内部长出来的。只有像 trademark 这样与借词成分构成的复合词才含拉丁来源的部分。

items.example: The bare stem serves as noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干兼作名词与动词。

items.example: The suffix turns the activity into a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把活动变成人。

items.example: The form names the ongoing activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式指持续进行的活动。

items.example: The suffix marks what may enter a market.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出什么可以进入市场。

items.example: The compound shifts from field to person.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词从领域移到人。

items.example: The compound loses the market sense entirely.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词完全丢掉了市场义。

items.example: Here trade means the business itself.
items.exampleCN: 此处 trade 指企业本身。

items.example: The compound keeps the oldest route sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词保留了最古老的路径义。

items.example: The adjective marks a policy, not a practice.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标出的是一项政策，而非一种做法。

definition_zh: 贸易路线；商路（连接产地与市场的固定运输与交易通道）
definition_en: a fixed path along which goods are carried between places that produce and places that consume them
core_image: 驼队沿一条被踩实的沙道走到山口，换过通行税后继续向前
scene: 山口的石屋里摆着一排陶罐，驼队在这里卸货、换税、再往西走。The trade route from the oasis to the coast has been walked for a thousand years.
sceneCN: 这里 trade route 指「连接产地与市场、固定运送货物的通道」（第 1 个义项：作为一条稳定的运输通道）；句意为从绿洲到海岸的这条商路已被走了上千年。

pos.zh: 贸易路线；商路（可数）

derivatives.zh: 中古低地德语 trade（路径）→ 贸易；交换（语义偏移：从路痕转指买卖）
古法语 rute（道路）→ 路线；按路线发送
re-（重新）+ route → 改道（语义偏移：换一条路径）
route + -ing → 路径安排；路由
route + -er → 路由器；镂铣机（语义偏移：择路之物）
法语 routine，同出 route → 常规；例行（语义偏移：固定的路成为固定的程序）

senses.title: Fixed path for carrying goods
senses.definition: a stable path along which goods are moved between producing and consuming regions
senses.definitionCN: 在产地与消费地之间稳定运送货物的路径
senses.example: The trade route from the oasis to the coast has been walked for a thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 从绿洲到海岸的这条商路已被走了上千年。
senses.why: Trade first meant a track, and route means a path broken through, so the compound is almost a tautology: the path of paths.
senses.whyCN: trade 本指足迹路径，route 指打通的道路，因此这个复合词几乎同义反复：路径的路径。

senses.title: Historic long-distance network
senses.titleCN: 历史上长距离的商路网络
senses.definition: a historical overland or combined network linking distant markets, such as the Silk Road
senses.definitionCN: 连接远方市场的历史陆路或混合网络，如丝绸之路
senses.example: Caravans on the old trade route carried silk west and glass east.
senses.exampleCN: 旧商路上的驼队把丝绸西运、把玻璃东运。
senses.why: A single path becomes a network once historians trace its branches and staging posts together.
senses.whyCN: 当史家把一条路径的各分支与驿站一并追溯，单条路径就成了网络。

senses.title: Sea lane used by shipping
senses.definition: a regular sea course followed by merchant ships between ports
senses.definitionCN: 商船在港口之间定期遵循的海上航路
senses.example: Pirates made the eastern trade route unsafe for small ships.
senses.exampleCN: 海盗使东部商路对小船变得不安全。
senses.why: Water has no visible road, so the route exists only as a repeated course between capes and straits.
senses.whyCN: 水上没有可见的路，航路只能作为在海角与海峡之间被反复走出的一条线路而存在。

senses.title: Modern freight corridor
senses.definition: a designated rail, road or pipeline corridor built to move freight between hubs
senses.definitionCN: 为在枢纽之间运送货物而划定的铁路、公路或管道走廊
senses.example: The new rail link turns the valley into a trade route for grain.
senses.exampleCN: 新的铁路连线使这条山谷成为粮食的货运通道。
senses.why: Once a route is engineered, the word moves from a worn path to an assigned corridor with a budget.
senses.whyCN: 一旦路线被工程建设，这个词就从踩出的路转为有预算的指定走廊。

senses.title: Path by which anything circulates
senses.titleCN: 任何东西流通的路径（比喻）
senses.definition: figuratively, the channel through which ideas, data or people travel and are exchanged
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指观念、数据或人在其中流动并被交换的渠道
senses.example: Scholars describe the journal as a trade route for ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 学者把这份期刊形容为观念流通的商路。
senses.why: If goods can have a route, anything carried and exchanged can borrow the same map.
senses.whyCN: 既然货品可以有路线，任何被运送与交换之物都能借用同一张地图。

senses.title: The itinerary of one trader
senses.definition: the sequence of stops that one merchant or caravan follows on a journey
senses.definitionCN: 某个商队或商人一次行商中所遵循的停留次序
senses.example: His trade route took him through four towns and back each season.
senses.exampleCN: 他的行商路线使他每季穿过四个城镇再返回。
senses.why: The compound can shrink from a public path to the private round of one seller.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词可从公共路径缩小为某个售卖者的私人循环。

senses.title: A corridor fixed by agreement
senses.titleCN: 由协议固定的过境通道
senses.definition: a transit corridor named in a trade or transit agreement, with agreed customs treatment
senses.definitionCN: 在贸易或过境协议中具名、享有约定海关待遇的通道
senses.example: The treaty made the river valley a licensed trade route.
senses.exampleCN: 条约使这条河谷成为受许可的贸易通道。
senses.why: Law turns a path into an institution: the route exists because documents say it does.
senses.whyCN: 法律把一条路径变成制度：通道之所以存在，是因为文件如此规定。

senses.title: A path reconstructed from finds
senses.titleCN: 由出土物推回出的路线
senses.definition: in archaeology, a route inferred from matching objects, coins and settlements rather than from written records
senses.definitionCN: 考古学中由器物、钱币与聚落的相互匹配、而非文献推回的路线
senses.example: Amber beads found inland mark a trade route that no map records.
senses.exampleCN: 内陆出土的琥珀珠标出一条任何地图都未记载的商路。
senses.why: Where no itinerary survives, the path must be rebuilt from what was carried along it.
senses.whyCN: 在没有行纪留存的地方，路径只能由沿途被携带的东西重建。

intro.en: Both halves of this compound are old words with independent histories, and the compound itself is a modern label for something ancient.
intro.cn: 这个复合词的两半都是有独立历史的老词，而复合词本身是给一件古老事物贴上的现代标签。

items.en: Trade meant 'track, course, path' and reached English in the fourteenth century; its commercial sense is later than the path sense.
items.cn: trade 意为「足迹、行程、路径」，十四世纪进入英语；其商业义晚于路径义。

items.en: Route comes from Old French rute 'road, way', the form that English borrowed in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: route 来自古法语 rute「道路、路程」，英语在十六世纪借入这一形式。

items.en: The French noun goes back to Latin rupta, short for via rupta 'a broken way', from rumpere 'to break'; a path is literally a way broken through the land.
items.cn: 这个法语名词回到拉丁 rupta，是 via rupta「被打通的路」的省略，出自 rumpere「打破」；路径字面上就是在大地上被打通的一条路。

items.en: Rumpere 'to break, burst' is the verb behind rupture and abrupt as well; the route is what is broken open for passage.
items.cn: rumpere「打破、破裂」也是 rupture 与 abrupt 背后的动词；route 即被破开以供通行的东西。

items.en: The compound trade route is recorded in English from the eighteenth century, when global shipping and colonial commerce needed a name for the paths between distant markets.
items.cn: 复合词 trade route 在英语中自十八世纪有记录，当时全球航运与殖民贸易需要给远方市场之间的路径一个名称。

items.en: Historians applied the label to older networks in the nineteenth century; Silk Road itself is a nineteenth-century coinage, so the name is newer than the road.
items.cn: 史家在十九世纪把这个标签用于更古老的网络；Silk Road 本身是十九世纪才造出的说法，因此名字比路更年轻。

note.en: The first group shares one half of the compound or its shape; the second holds terms for the same kind of channel.
note.cn: 第一组共享复合词的一半或其外形；第二组是同一类通道的其他说法。

entries.definition: The first element alone names commerce or an occupation; it says nothing about a route.
entries.definitionCN: 只取第一个成分时指贸易或行业，完全不含路线之义。

entries.definition: The second element alone names any way from one point to another, including a bus route or a delivery route.
entries.definitionCN: 只取第二个成分时指任何从一处到另一处的路径，包括公交线路、送货路线。

entries.definition: Built the same way but marked for water; a sea route may or may not be a trade route.
entries.definitionCN: 同型构成，但标出的是水域；海上航路未必就是商路。

entries.definition: The process of choosing or directing a path, used for networks, parcels and data rather than for caravans.
entries.definitionCN: 选择或指派路径的过程，多用于网络、包裹与数据，而非驼队。

entries.definition: A set of linked routes and markets rather than a single line; historians prefer it for the Silk Road system.
entries.definitionCN: 一组相连的路线与市场，而非单条线路；史家更愿用它称丝绸之路体系。

entries.definition: A planned strip of land or water reserved for movement, often with legal status; a trade route may be informal and old.
entries.definitionCN: 为通行划定的陆上或水上带状区域，常带法律地位；商路则可能古老而不正式。

entries.definition: A charted channel used by ships, often defined for traffic separation; the emphasis is navigation, not commerce.
entries.definitionCN: 海图上标出的航道，常为分道通航而划定；侧重点是航行而非商业。

entries.definition: A route worked by pack animals in stages; it specifies the means of transport where trade route does not.
entries.definitionCN: 靠驮畜分段行走的路线；它指明运输方式，而 trade route 不指明。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: trade 'track' plus route 'broken way': the worn path of goods.
normal.cn: trade「足迹路径」加 route「打通的路」：货物走过的旧路。

normal.en: The two halves each stand alone: trade is the business, route is the way.
normal.cn: 两半都能独立：trade 是生意，route 是路。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the type: ancient trade route, maritime trade route, a trade route between cities.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类型：古代商路、海上商路、城市之间的商路。

normal.en: The Silk Road is the most famous example, and its name is younger than the road.
normal.cn: 丝绸之路是最著名的例子，而这个名字比路本身更年轻。

normal.en: Historians also say trade network when they mean many routes at once.
normal.cn: 史家要指多条路线同时存在时，也说 trade network。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn in sand by ten thousand feet, then used by mapmakers as if it were a border.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被上万只脚在沙上踩出的线，后来被绘图者当作边界来用。

abstract.en: Picture a customs house standing alone at a pass, the route existing because someone can tax it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座孤零零立在山口的关卡，路之所以成为路，是因为有人能对它征税。

abstract.en: Picture amber beads inland, redrawing a road no book ever wrote down.
abstract.cn: 想象内陆的琥珀珠，重新画出一条从没有书提过的路。

examples.en: Merchants avoided the northern trade route in winter because the passes closed.
examples.cn: 商人冬天避开北方商路，因为山口会封。

examples.en: The city grew rich by controlling the trade route between the mountains and the sea.
examples.cn: 这座城市靠控制山与海之间的商路而致富。

examples.en: Archaeologists traced a trade route from the distribution of the same clay lamps.
examples.cn: 考古学家依据同一种陶灯的分布推出一条商路。

dict_mnemonic.text: trade（贸易）+ route（路线）＝ 货物走惯的那条路；记「有人走、有人税、有人记」。

root: trade 来自中古低地德语「足迹、路径」；route 来自古法语 rute，追溯至拉丁 rupta（via rupta「被打通的路」，出自 rumpere「打破」）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a walked path to a legal corridor: the fixed channel, the historic network, the sea lane, the engineered corridor, the figurative channel, one trader's round, the treaty corridor, and the route rebuilt from broken objects.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一条被走出的路延伸到一条法律走廊：固定通道、历史网络、海上航路、工程走廊、比喻渠道、单个商人的行程、条约通道，以及从残片重建的路线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: goods leaving one place and arriving at another along a line that outlasts both the goods and the people carrying them.
core.cn: 核心意象：货物沿一条线离开一地、抵达另一地，而这条线比货物与运货的人活得都久。

branches.en: PUBLIC PATH AND PRIVATE ROUND: the same line serves a whole trade and one trader's season.
branches.cn: 公共路径与私人循环：同一条线既服务整个贸易，也服务一个商人的一季。

branches.en: RECORDED AND RECONSTRUCTED: historians trace it in documents, archaeologists rebuild it from what was carried.
branches.cn: 有记录与靠重建：史家依文献追溯，考古学家依被携带之物重建。

branches.en: WATER AND STEEL: the lane exists as a repeated course, the corridor as an engineered strip.
branches.cn: 水与钢：航路作为反复行走的线路存在，走廊作为被工程化的地带存在。

branches.en: ANYTHING THAT CIRCULATES: ideas and data borrow the map once goods have shown how to draw it.
branches.cn: 任何流通之物：货品示范了如何画图之后，观念与数据便借用这张图。

branches.en: THE PATH AS AN INSTITUTION: a treaty can create a route simply by naming it.
branches.cn: 路径即制度：条约只需点名，就能造出一条商路。

intro.en: The compound is made of two free words, each of which still carries its own family, so the whole can be read as a phrase as well as a term.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由两个自由词构成，每个词都自带词族，因此整体既可读作短语，也可读作术语。

latinIntro.en: Only the second half has a Latin ancestry, through French rute from Latin rupta; the first half is Germanic and means a track. Nothing here is borrowed whole from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后半有拉丁来历，经法语 rute 回到拉丁 rupta；前半属日耳曼语，意为足迹路径。这里没有整体借自拉丁的成分。

items.example: The first element supplies the purpose of the path.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分提供这条路径的用途。

items.example: The second element supplies the path itself.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分提供路径本身。

items.example: The prefix reverses the chosen line.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把已选的线路改向。

items.example: The form names the act rather than the line.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式指动作而非线路。

items.example: The suffix makes an agent out of a path.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把路径变成施动者。

items.meaning: a fixed way of doing things
items.example: A fixed path becomes a fixed procedure.
items.exampleCN: 固定的路径变成固定的程序。

items.example: The pattern repeats with a different medium.
items.exampleCN: 同一模式换上另一种介质。

items.example: The compound widens one line into many.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把一条线扩成多条。

items.example: The compound adds the means of carriage.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词补上运输方式。

latinEntries.meaning: a broken way, an opened road

definition_zh: 商业；贸易；（大规模、跨地区的）买卖活动；往来交流
definition_en: the buying and selling of goods and services on a large scale, especially between regions
core_image: 港口仓库里堆满待发的木箱，吊机把货从船腹提到岸上，账房在门口逐箱核对
scene: 海关大厅里，报关员把一叠单据逐页盖章放行，集装箱在门外排成长队。Commerce between the two regions stalled for a month after the bridge closed.
sceneCN: 这里 commerce 指「跨地区的大规模买卖活动」（第 1 个义项：作为区域间的整体贸易）；句意为桥断之后，两地之间的商业停顿了一个月。

pos.zh: 商业；贸易（不可数）；往来、交流（旧义）

collocations.zh: 与远方港口的贸易往来

derivatives.zh: commerce + -ial（形容词后缀）→ 商业的；电视广告（语义偏移：从活动转到媒介产物）
commercial + -ize（使…化）→ 商业化
commercialize + -ation（过程）→ 商业化过程
拉丁 mercari（做买卖）+ -ant（人）→ 商人（与 commerce 同出 merx，但走的是人称那条线）
merchant + -ise（名词后缀）→ 商品；推销（语义偏移：从人转到货）
意大利 mercante + -ile → 重商主义的；贸易的

senses.title: Large-scale trade between regions
senses.definition: the buying and selling of goods and services on a large scale, especially across distance
senses.definitionCN: 大规模买卖货物与服务，尤指跨距离进行
senses.example: Commerce between the two regions stalled for a month after the bridge closed.
senses.exampleCN: 桥断之后，两地之间的商业停顿了一个月。
senses.why: Latin commercium joined com- 'together' with merx 'merchandise', so the word begins as goods being handled together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 commercium 把 com-「共同」与 merx「货物」合在一起，因此这个词最初就是货物被共同经手。

senses.title: The business sector dealing in goods
senses.titleCN: 从事货品交易的商业部门
senses.definition: the part of an economy concerned with buying and selling, as opposed to agriculture or labour
senses.definitionCN: 经济中负责买卖的部分，与农业或劳工相对
senses.example: The town lives on commerce rather than on what it grows.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城镇靠商业而不是靠本地出产过活。
senses.why: An activity becomes a sector once statistics and ministries need to count it separately.
senses.whyCN: 当统计与行政部门需要把它单独计数，活动就变成一个部门。

senses.title: Trade as a formal institution
senses.definition: the organized system of exchange, with its law, credit and ports, treated as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 被视为制度的有组织交换体系，含法律、信贷与港口
senses.example: Medieval commerce depended on bills of exchange that no king had to honour.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的商业依赖无需国王担保的汇票。
senses.why: The formal register of the word fits institutions: one says commerce in treaties, trade in shops.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的正式语域适配制度：条约里说 commerce，店铺里说 trade。

senses.title: Interchange of ideas or feelings
senses.definition: archaic or literary: communication and exchange between minds or groups
senses.definitionCN: 旧义或书面语：思想与群体之间的沟通与交换
senses.example: The essay praises commerce between scholars of different tongues.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章称赞不同语言的学者之间的往来。
senses.why: Before it meant goods, commerce meant dealings between people; the abstract sense survives in literary use.
senses.whyCN: 在指货物之前，commerce 指人与人之间的交往；这一抽象义留在书面语里。

senses.title: Transactions through an online platform
senses.titleCN: 通过线上平台完成的交易
senses.definition: buying and selling conducted through websites or apps, often shortened to e-commerce
senses.definitionCN: 通过网站或应用进行的买卖，常缩略为电子商务
senses.example: Commerce moved to the phone, and the high street emptied.
senses.exampleCN: 交易转到了手机上，商业街便空了。
senses.why: The medium changes while the underlying act stays the same, so no new noun is needed.
senses.whyCN: 介质变了，底层的动作没变，因此不需要另造名词。

senses.title: Industry and trade taken as one body
senses.titleCN: 把工商界视为一个整体
senses.definition: the collective body of firms and traders, often paired with labour or government
senses.definitionCN: 企业与商人的整体，常与劳工或政府并列
senses.example: The report was written for commerce, not for the workers it describes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是写给工商界看的，而不是写给它所描述的工人的。
senses.why: Metonymy again: the activity stands for the people who carry it on.
senses.whyCN: 仍是转喻：活动代表从事这项活动的人。

senses.title: Movement of goods, in older usage
senses.definition: dated: the traffic or passage of goods, including the vehicles and routes that carry them
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：货物的运输往来，含承运的车船与路线
senses.example: The old canal was built for commerce, not for pleasure boats.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧运河是为货运而建，不是为游船。
senses.why: Where goods move, the word can name the movement itself, a sense now largely taken over by traffic.
senses.whyCN: 货物流动之处，这个词可指流动本身，这一义项如今大体被 traffic 接管。

senses.title: Any two-way interchange
senses.definition: figuratively, a continuing two-way exchange of anything, such as letters, data or insults
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指任何事物持续的双向交换，如书信、数据或互相辱骂
senses.example: There was little commerce between the two departments all year.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个部门整年几乎没有往来。
senses.why: Once exchange is the core, the objects exchanged can be anything at all.
senses.whyCN: 一旦核心是「交换」，被交换的东西就可以是任何一种。

intro.en: Commerce is a Latin noun built from a prefix and a noun for goods, and it reached English through French with its large-scale, institutional tone already attached.
intro.cn: commerce 是一个由前缀与表「货物」的名词构成的拉丁词，经法语进入英语时，大规模与制度化的语气已经附着在上面。

items.en: Merx, genitive mercis, meant 'merchandise, goods'. Its own origin is uncertain; suggestions linking it to a trading root remain hypotheses rather than demonstrated derivations.
items.cn: merx（属格 mercis）意为「货物、商品」。它自身的来源不确定；把它与某个表「交易」的词根相联系的说法仍属假说，而非已证实的派生。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus merx produced commercium 'trade, traffic, intercourse', literally goods handled together.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 merx 构成 commercium「贸易、往来、交流」，字面即货物被共同经手。

items.en: Old French took the Latin noun as commerce and widened it to mean dealings of any kind between people.
items.cn: 古法语把这个拉丁名词接为 commerce，并将其扩大到人与人之间任何性质的交往。

items.en: English borrows the word in the sixteenth century; early uses still include conversation and correspondence as well as trade.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个词；早期用法除贸易外仍包括交谈与通信。

items.en: With chambers of commerce and colonial shipping, the word settles into its modern sense of large-scale organized trade.
items.cn: 随着商会与殖民航运的出现，这个词落定于现代义：大规模、有组织的贸易。

items.en: Electronic commerce and e-commerce extend the same noun to transactions completed without a shared building or a handshake.
items.cn: 电子商务与 e-commerce 把同一个名词扩展到无需同一座建筑、无需握手的交易。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same goods root or on a misleadingly similar shape; the second holds terms that overlap in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「货物」词根、或外形相近而易误认的词；第二组是意思重叠的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective of commerce; as a noun it means a television advertisement, a sense the base noun does not have.
entries.definitionCN: commerce 的形容词；作名词时指电视广告，这是原名词没有的义项。

entries.definition: Built on the same merx but through mercari 'to trade'; it names the trader, not the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 merx，但经 mercari「做买卖」而来；它指商人，而非贸易活动。

entries.definition: From Italian mercante, describing trade or a policy devoted to trade profits rather than to the activity itself.
entries.definitionCN: 来自意大利 mercante，描述贸易事务或唯贸易利益是图的政策，而非活动本身。

entries.definition: Nothing to do with goods: it comes from com- plus initiare 'to begin', and it means to start.
entries.definitionCN: 与货物无关：来自 com- 加 initiare「开始」，意为着手、开始。

entries.definition: The everyday word, covering both large and small dealing and also an occupation; commerce is formal and large-scale.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用词，大小交易皆可，还指行业；commerce 正式且指大规模。

entries.definition: Any commercial activity or enterprise, including services; commerce usually means goods moving between regions.
entries.definitionCN: 任何商业活动或企业，含服务业；commerce 通常指货品在区域间流动。

entries.definition: The movement of goods or people, often suggesting volume and sometimes illicit dealing, as in drug traffic.
entries.definitionCN: 货物或人的流动，常含数量之意，有时指非法交易，如毒品贩运。

entries.definition: The promotion and presentation of goods for sale, a narrow part of commerce rather than the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 为出售而做的货品推广与陈列，是商业的一小部分，而非整个体系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: com- 'together' + merx 'goods': goods handled together, which is trade.
normal.cn: com-「共同」+ merx「货物」：货物被共同经手，这就是贸易。

normal.en: The family runs commerce, commercial, commercialize, merchant, merchandise, mercantile.
normal.cn: 同族词有 commerce、commercial、commercialize、merchant、merchandise、mercantile。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the institutional tone: chamber of commerce, international commerce, commerce and industry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出制度化语气：商会、国际贸易、工商界。

normal.en: The word is formal where trade is plain: treaties say commerce, shops say trade.
normal.cn: 这个词正式，而 trade 平实：条约里说 commerce，店铺里说 trade。

normal.en: The old sense survives in writing: commerce between minds means correspondence and conversation.
normal.cn: 旧义仍留在书面语中：commerce between minds 指通信与交谈。

abstract.en: Picture a warehouse where every crate is counted twice, once by the seller and once by the buyer.
abstract.cn: 想象一间仓库，每只木箱都被数两遍，卖者一遍，买者一遍。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge carrying carts of goods; when it closes, the word for trade stops being abstract.
abstract.cn: 想象一座载着货车的桥；桥一断，那个指贸易的词就不再抽象。

abstract.en: Picture two scholars writing letters for forty years and calling it commerce.
abstract.cn: 想象两位学者通信四十年，并把这称作 commerce。

examples.en: The city grew rich on commerce long before it had a university.
examples.cn: 这座城市靠商业致富，远在它有大学之前。

examples.en: Commerce has moved online, but the warehouse is still the size of a cathedral.
examples.cn: 商业已转到线上，但仓库仍有大教堂那么大。

examples.en: The treaty protects commerce on the river for all signatories.
examples.cn: 条约保护所有签署国在这条河上的商业往来。

dict_mnemonic.text: com（共同）+ merce（货物，源自 merx）＝ 大家一起搬货做买卖；比 trade 更正式、更大型。

root: 拉丁 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」+ com-「共同」→ commercium「贸易、往来」→ 古法语 commerce；merx 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses widen from a counted crate to a whole sector: regional trade, the trading sector, the institution, the old sense of intercourse, the online platform, the collective industry, the movement of goods, and any two-way exchange.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一只被清点的木箱扩展到整个部门：区域贸易、商业部门、制度、旧义的往来、线上平台、工商整体、货物流动，以及任何双向交流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many hands moving the same goods, each hand believing it will gain by the deal.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多双手在搬同一批货物，每双手都相信自己会因这笔交易而得利。

branches.en: ACTIVITY AND SECTOR: first the dealing itself, then the part of the economy that lives by it.
branches.cn: 活动与部门：先是买卖本身，再是靠它吃饭的那部分经济。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND MOVEMENT: law and credit make trade an institution, and the carriage of goods is its physical half.
branches.cn: 制度与流动：法律与信贷把贸易变成制度，货物运输则是它的实体一半。

branches.en: DEALINGS WITHOUT GOODS: the oldest sense of intercourse survives for letters, ideas and departmental contact.
branches.cn: 不经货物的往来：最古老的交往义留存于书信、观念与部门间的接触。

branches.en: A NEW MEDIUM: the platform removes the shared building but not the act.
branches.cn: 新的介质：平台取消了共同的建筑，却没有取消那个动作。

branches.en: PEOPLE AS THE SECTOR: the activity stands for the firms that carry it on, as when a report is written for commerce.
branches.cn: 以人代部门：活动代表从事它的企业，如报告写给工商界看时。

intro.en: Commerce is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin noun of goods, and both parts recur across a large English family.
intro.cn: commerce 由一个拉丁前缀与一个表货物的拉丁名词构成，两部分在一个庞大的英语词族中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin merx 'goods' gives merchant, merchandise, mercantile and market through mercari and mercatus; com- adds the idea of doing something together. The two strands meet again in commerce.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 merx「货物」经 mercari 与 mercatus 给出 merchant、merchandise、mercantile 与 market；com- 增添「共同进行」之意。两条线在 commerce 再次汇合。

items.example: The prefix binds the dealing into one shared act.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把交易绑成一个共同行为。

items.example: The noun supplies the objects of the trade.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供交易的对象。

items.example: The compound is the abstract activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是抽象的活动。

items.example: The suffix turns activity into a property.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把活动变成属性。

items.meaning: to make a thing into a market
items.example: The verb moves trade into new domains.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把贸易推进新的领域。

items.example: The person form takes the same goods root.
items.exampleCN: 人称形式用的是同一个货物词根。

items.example: The word moves from the trader back to the goods.
items.exampleCN: 这个词又从商人回到货物。

items.example: The form came through Italian rather than French.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式是经意大利语而非法语来的。

items.meaning: a place or state of trading
items.example: The same root gives the place where commerce happens.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根给出商业发生的场所。

latinEntries.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (verb, first conjugation, deponent)

definition_zh: 商人；（批发的）货商；酒商、煤炭商等专营商人；商船的
definition_en: a person or firm that buys and sells goods, especially in large quantities or across borders
core_image: 码头仓库门口，一个穿长外套的人对着账本清点整匹的布，身后是刚卸下的货堆
scene: 码头仓库里，收货人掀开帆布，逐匹检查刚卸下的丝绸，账本上记着欠款与运费。The merchant sold silk by the bale and never dealt in single bolts.
sceneCN: 这里 merchant 指「以大宗货物跨地买卖为业的人」（第 1 个义项：作为从事大宗贸易的商人）；句意为这位商人按整包卖丝绸，从不拆成单匹零售。

pos.zh: 商人；批发商；专营商人
商船的；商业的（多见于 merchant ship、merchant navy）

derivatives.zh: merchant + -ise（名词后缀）→ 商品；推销（语义偏移：从人转到货）
merchandise + -ing（动名词）→ 货品推广与陈列
merchant + -able（可…的）→ 适销的（法律用语）
merchant + man → 商船（语义偏移：从人转到船）
意大利 mercante + -ile → 贸易的；重商的
com- + merx → 商业（同根，走抽象活动那条线）

senses.title: Trader in goods, especially wholesale
senses.titleCN: 从事货物买卖的商人（尤指批发）
senses.definition: a person or firm that buys goods in quantity and sells them on, often across distance
senses.definitionCN: 成批买进再转售的个人或企业，常跨距离经营
senses.example: The merchant sold silk by the bale and never dealt in single bolts.
senses.exampleCN: 这位商人按整包卖丝绸，从不拆成单匹零售。
senses.why: Latin mercari 'to trade' plus the person suffix -ant gives the one who trades, and the word keeps the bulk-dealing sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 mercari「做买卖」加人称后缀 -ant 给出「做买卖的人」，而这个词保留了成批交易之义。

senses.title: A shopkeeper, in older British use
senses.definition: dated: a retail shopkeeper, especially one who owns the shop
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：零售店主，尤指店铺所有者
senses.example: The village merchant knew every family's account by heart.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的店主把每家的账都记在心里。
senses.why: Before chain stores, the local shopkeeper was simply the person who traded, so the word needed no qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 在连锁店出现之前，本地店主就是做买卖的那个人，因此这个词无需限定语。

senses.title: Dealer in one commodity
senses.titleCN: 某一类货品的专营商人
senses.definition: a specialist dealer whose trade is named with the word, as a wine merchant or coal merchant
senses.definitionCN: 以本词构成称谓的专营商人，如酒商、煤商
senses.example: The wine merchant will not open a bottle that has not rested a year.
senses.exampleCN: 那位酒商不肯开一瓶还没放满一年的酒。
senses.why: The compound pattern merchant of X narrows the general trader to one stock.
senses.whyCN: 「X + merchant」这一复合模式把一般商人收窄到一种货品。

senses.title: Wholesaler supplying retailers
senses.titleCN: 向零售商供货的批发商
senses.definition: a middle trader who buys from producers and supplies shops rather than end customers
senses.definitionCN: 从生产者买进、供给店铺而非最终顾客的中间商
senses.example: Retailers complained that the merchant kept the best lots for himself.
senses.exampleCN: 零售商抱怨那位批发商把最好的货留给了自己。
senses.why: Scale separates the merchant from the shop: one moves cases, the other sells units.
senses.whyCN: 规模把 merchant 与店铺分开：一个搬整箱，一个卖单件。

senses.title: Member of a chartered trading company
senses.definition: historical: a member of a company granted a monopoly of trade with a region
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法：获得某地区贸易垄断权的公司成员
senses.example: A merchant of the company could lose his charter for private dealing.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司的商人若私自交易，会被吊销特许状。
senses.why: Charters turned merchants into licensed agents of a state, and the word absorbed that status.
senses.whyCN: 特许状把商人变成国家的受许代理人，这个词也就吸收了那层身份。

senses.title: One who trades in something abstract
senses.titleCN: 经营抽象之物的人（比喻）
senses.definition: figuratively, a person who circulates a quality or a commodity that is not goods, as a merchant of doubt
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指流通某种非货物之物的人，如散布疑虑者
senses.example: He is a merchant of doubt, paid by the column and never by the fact.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个贩卖疑虑的人，按专栏收钱，从不按事实收钱。
senses.why: If goods can be sold, anything marketable can be sold, so the person noun travels with them.
senses.whyCN: 既然货物能卖，任何可售之物都能卖，指人的名词便随之而去。

senses.title: Attributive use for shipping
senses.definition: used before nouns to mark vessels or fleets that carry commercial cargo rather than troops
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标出载运商业货物而非军队的船只或船队
senses.example: The merchant fleet was requisitioned before the war began.
senses.exampleCN: 战争开始前，商船队就被征用了。
senses.why: A trader on land becomes a ship at sea, and the noun works as a plain classifier.
senses.whyCN: 陆上的商人在海上成了船，这个名词便充当简单的分类语。

senses.title: Promoter of something unwelcome
senses.titleCN: 推销不受欢迎之物的人
senses.definition: in modern compounds, a person who promotes a bad thing as if selling it, as a doom merchant
senses.definitionCN: 在现代复合词中，指把坏东西当作货品来推销的人，如唱衰者
senses.example: The paper calls every forecaster a doom merchant.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸把每个预测者都叫作唱衰者。
senses.why: The selling frame is so strong that it can be attached to ideas nobody wants to buy.
senses.whyCN: 兜售这一框架太强，以至于可以挂到没人想买的主张上。

intro.en: Merchant is the person-shaped member of the goods family: the same Latin noun for merchandise, put through a verb of trading and a French suffix for people.
intro.cn: merchant 是「货物」词族中取人形的那个成员：同一个表商品的拉丁名词，经一个表交易的动词与一个法语人称后缀而成。

items.en: Merx, genitive mercis, meant 'merchandise, goods'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the links sometimes proposed to a trading root are hypotheses, not established derivations.
items.cn: merx（属格 mercis）意为「货物、商品」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出的与某个交易词根的联系只是假说，并非已成立的派生。

items.en: Mercari 'to trade, to deal' is the deponent verb built on merx; it supplies the stem that carries the person suffix.
items.cn: mercari「做买卖、交易」是建于 merx 之上的异态动词，提供了承载人称后缀的词干。

items.en: Mercator 'trader' is the direct Latin person noun, and it survives in English in learned and historical writing.
items.cn: mercator「商人」是直接的拉丁人称名词，在英语的学术与历史写作中仍可见到。

items.en: Old French marchant names a trader or shopkeeper and is the form English borrowed, with the -ch- that English later reduced.
items.cn: 古法语 marchant 指商人或店主，是英语借入的形式，其中的 -ch- 后来在英语里弱化。

items.en: Early English spellings vary between marchaunt and merchant; the word covers both the long-distance trader and the local shopkeeper.
items.cn: 早期英语拼写在 marchaunt 与 merchant 之间摆动；这个词同时涵盖长途商人与本地店主。

items.en: Modern English separates merchant from shopkeeper and keeps the word for wholesale, specialist and shipping uses; the compound patterns wine merchant and doom merchant show both ends of that range.
items.cn: 现代英语把 merchant 与店主分开，保留批发、专营与航运用法；wine merchant 与 doom merchant 这两个复合模式正显出这一区间的两端。

note.en: The first group shares the goods root or the shape; the second holds words for the people who sell at different points in the chain.
note.cn: 第一组共享货物词根或外形；第二组是销售链条不同环节上的人。

entries.definition: The noun for goods bought and sold, formed from merchant; it names the cargo, not the trader.
entries.definitionCN: 指买卖的货物，由 merchant 构成；它指货，不指人。

entries.definition: Describing trade or a policy bent on profit; it came through Italian and has no plural or person form.
entries.definitionCN: 描述贸易或唯利是图的政策；经意大利语而来，无人称或复数形式。

entries.definition: A commercial-law word meaning fit to be sold, said of goods rather than of people.
entries.definitionCN: 商法用词，意为适销，说的是货物而非人。

entries.definition: The abstract noun of trade; merchant is the person who carries it on.
entries.definitionCN: 指贸易的抽象名词；merchant 是从事贸易的人。

entries.definition: Anyone who trades, including a market stall or a brokerage desk; merchant sounds older and grander.
entries.definitionCN: 任何做交易的人，包括市场摊位或经纪台；merchant 显得更老派、更有分量。

entries.definition: A specialist buyer and seller, as a car dealer or an art dealer; merchant often implies bulk and distance.
entries.definitionCN: 某一商品或市场的专营买卖者，如汽车经销商、艺术品经销商；merchant 常含大宗与跨地之意。

entries.definition: A trader who sells to shops rather than to households; the word names a position, not a tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 卖给店铺而非住户的商人；这个词标出链条位置，而非一种传统。

entries.definition: The person behind a shop counter; it fixes the word to one premises, which merchant never does.
entries.definitionCN: 站在店铺柜台后的人；它把人固定在某一处店面，而 merchant 从不这样限定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: merx 'goods' + -ant 'person': the person of goods.
normal.cn: merx「货物」+ -ant「人」：货物的人。

normal.en: The family runs merchant, merchandise, merchandising, merchantable, merchantman, mercantile, commerce.
normal.cn: 同族词有 merchant、merchandise、merchandising、merchantable、merchantman、mercantile、commerce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark specialities: wine merchant, coal merchant, merchant bank, merchant ship.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出专营：酒商、煤商、商人银行、商船。

normal.en: The word moved from person to cargo: merchant sells merchandise.
normal.cn: 这个词从人走到货：merchant 卖 merchandise。

normal.en: Merchantman is a ship, not a man, a reminder that the suffix once meant a vessel.
normal.cn: merchantman 是船而非人，提醒人们这个后缀曾指船只。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger in which every page is a debt and every debt is a bale of cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账册，每一页是一笔欠款，每笔欠款是一包布。

abstract.en: Picture a charter that turns a private trader into an arm of the state.
abstract.cn: 想象一份特许状，把私人商人变成国家的一只手臂。

abstract.en: Picture a newspaper column written by someone who sells fear by the word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按字出售恐惧的人所写的报纸专栏。

examples.en: A merchant from Genoa financed the voyage and took a third of the cargo.
examples.cn: 一位热那亚商人资助了这次航行，并取走三分之一的货。

examples.en: The coal merchant delivers on Wednesdays and will not come for a single sack.
examples.cn: 煤商每周三送货，不会为一袋煤专门跑一趟。

examples.en: Merchant ships were stopped and searched for contraband.
examples.cn: 商船被拦下搜查违禁品。

dict_mnemonic.text: merce（货物）＋ ant（人）＝ 管货物的人；记「整包进、整包出，账本不离手」。

root: 拉丁 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」→ mercari「做买卖」→ 拉丁 mercator「商人」→ 古法语 marchant → 英语 merchant；merx 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one trader through the chain: bulk dealer, local shopkeeper, single-commodity specialist, wholesaler, chartered agent, dealer in abstractions, shipping classifier, and promoter of bad news.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个商人沿链条走一遍：大宗商、本地店主、单一货品专营者、批发商、受特许的代理人、抽象之物的经营者、航运的分类语，以及坏消息的推销者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger, a bale and a long walk between the quay and the shop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本账册、一包货，以及码头与店铺之间那段长路。

branches.en: BULK AND COUNTER: the same trader scaled down to a village shop before chain stores existed.
branches.cn: 大宗与柜台：同一个商人在连锁店出现之前缩小为村里的店铺。

branches.en: SPECIALITY AND POSITION: one stock only, and a place in the chain between maker and shop.
branches.cn: 专营与位置：只做一种货，并在制作者与店铺之间占一个环节。

branches.en: LICENSED TRADER: a charter converts private dealing into a granted monopoly.
branches.cn: 受许商人：特许状把私人交易转为授予的垄断。

branches.en: ANYTHING SELLABLE: doubt and doom can be stocked and sold like cloth.
branches.cn: 任何可售之物：疑虑与唱衰也能像布匹一样囤积出售。

branches.en: OUTWARD FORMS: at sea the trader becomes a ship, in print a seller of bad news.
branches.cn: 外在形态：在海上商人成船，在纸面上成为坏消息的售卖者。

intro.en: Merchant is a Latin goods noun plus a Latin person suffix, filtered through French; the same root builds the words for goods, for trade policy and for the market itself.
intro.cn: merchant 是一个拉丁货物名词加一个拉丁人称后缀，经法语过滤而成；同一词根还构成指商品、指贸易政策与指市场本身的词。

latinIntro.en: From merx come mercari 'to trade', mercator 'trader', mercatus 'market' and commercium 'trade together'; English draws merchant, merchandise and commerce from that single stock.
latinIntro.cn: 由 merx 生出 mercari「交易」、mercator「商人」、mercatus「市场」与 commercium「共同交易」；英语从这一处取来 merchant、merchandise 与 commerce。

items.example: The root names what is traded.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被交易的东西。

items.example: The verb supplies the stem before the person suffix.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词在人称后缀之前提供词干。

items.example: The person form is the everyday English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个人体形式就是日常英语中的这个词。

items.example: The suffix returns the word to the cargo.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词带回货物。

items.example: The form names the selling work around the goods.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式指围绕货品的销售工作。

items.example: The suffix creates a legal standard for goods.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀为货物造出一条法律标准。

items.example: Here man means vessel, not person.
items.exampleCN: 此处 man 指船只，不指人。

items.example: The Italian route gives a separate adjective.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语这条路径给出另一个形容词。

items.example: The abstract member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 家族中的抽象成员。

items.example: The same stock names where the dealing happens.
items.exampleCN: 同一词源指交易发生之处。
