definition_zh: 集市；市场；（观念、产品）竞争与交易的场所；线上交易平台
definition_en: an open area where goods are sold, or any setting in which goods, services or ideas compete for buyers
core_image: 广场上一排布棚，摊主把菜摆成整齐的堆，买的人在两排摊位之间来回比较
scene: 周末的广场上，摊主支起布棚，买菜的人挤在鱼摊前讨价还价。The marketplace opens at six, when farmers bring in whatever survived the frost.
sceneCN: 这里 marketplace 指「摊贩聚集、公开买卖的露天场所」（第 1 个义项：作为实体的集市广场）；句意为集市六点开门，农夫把霜后剩下的东西都运来。

pos.zh: 集市；市场（可数）；竞争场所

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 mercatus（交易、市场）→ 市场；推销
market + -ing → 营销（语义偏移：从场所转到活动）
market + -er → 营销人员
market + -able → 适销的
market 的缩略 → 集市（旧用法）
super-（在上）+ market → 超市（语义偏移：从露天场到自选店）

senses.title: An open square where stalls sell
senses.definition: a public open area where traders set up stalls and buyers come to buy
senses.definitionCN: 商贩摆摊、买者前来采购的公共露天场地
senses.example: The marketplace opens at six, when farmers bring in whatever survived the frost.
senses.exampleCN: 集市六点开门，农夫把霜后剩下的东西都运来。
senses.why: Market came from Latin mercatus 'trade, market', and place from Latin platea 'broad street', so the compound is literally a trading square.
senses.whyCN: market 来自拉丁 mercatus「交易、市场」，place 来自拉丁 platea「宽阔的街」，因此这个复合词字面上就是一块交易广场。

senses.title: The world of commercial competition
senses.definition: the abstract arena in which firms compete for customers, as in enter the marketplace
senses.definitionCN: 企业争夺顾客的抽象场域，如「进入市场」
senses.example: A new brand cannot survive long in a crowded marketplace.
senses.exampleCN: 新品牌在拥挤的市场里撑不了多久。
senses.why: The physical square stands for the whole arena where buyers can be won or lost.
senses.whyCN: 实体的广场代表整个可能赢得或失去买主的场域。

senses.title: An online platform for buying and selling
senses.definition: a website or app where many sellers list goods and many buyers purchase them
senses.definitionCN: 许多卖家挂货、许多买家下单的网站或应用
senses.example: The marketplace takes a commission on every sale.
senses.exampleCN: 这个平台对每笔交易抽取佣金。
senses.why: The square is rebuilt in software: stalls become listings, and the crowd becomes traffic.
senses.whyCN: 广场在软件里被重建：摊位成了商品页，人群成了流量。

senses.title: A place reserved for one trade
senses.definition: a building or area given over to one kind of dealing, as a fish market or a flower market
senses.definitionCN: 专供某一类买卖的建筑或区域，如鱼市、花市
senses.example: The fish marketplace behind the harbour starts work at three.
senses.exampleCN: 港口后面的鱼市三点就开始干活。
senses.why: One commodity can claim a whole square, and the compound follows the same pattern as market.
senses.whyCN: 一种货品就能占满一整块场地，复合词与 market 遵循同一模式。

senses.title: The available demand for a product
senses.definition: the set of buyers willing to purchase a particular product, treated as a place to be found
senses.definitionCN: 愿意购买某产品的买者整体，被当作一个可被找到的场所
senses.example: The device found a marketplace among rural clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 这种设备在农村诊所找到了市场。
senses.why: Demand is spoken of spatially: you enter it, find it, or are pushed out of it.
senses.whyCN: 需求被空间化地表述：你进入它、找到它，或被挤出它。

senses.title: A town's right to hold a market
senses.titleCN: 城镇举办集市的特许权
senses.definition: historical: the charter right of a town to hold a regular market, with tolls and rules
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法：城镇定期举办集市、收取通行税并立规矩的特许权
senses.example: The charter granted the marketplace and the tolls that came with it.
senses.exampleCN: 特许状授予集市本身，以及随之而来的通行税。
senses.why: A market was a legal privilege before it was a location, so the word can mean the right itself.
senses.whyCN: 集市在被当作地点之前先是一项法律特权，因此这个词也可指权利本身。

senses.title: An arena of public argument
senses.definition: figuratively, a setting where ideas or claims are offered and weighed by an audience
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指各种主张被提出并由受众权衡的场域
senses.example: The letters page became a marketplace for rival histories.
senses.exampleCN: 读者来信版成了相互竞争的史观的集市。
senses.why: If buyers choose among goods, readers choose among arguments, and the same word serves.
senses.whyCN: 若买主在货物间挑选，读者便在论点间挑选，同一个词便可用。

senses.title: A platform business model
senses.definition: an attributive use marking businesses that host transactions rather than own stock
senses.definitionCN: 定语用法，标出撮合交易而不自持库存的企业
senses.example: Marketplace lending bypasses the branch and the teller.
senses.exampleCN: 平台型借贷绕过了支行与柜员。
senses.why: The noun becomes a classifier for a model, showing how far a word for a square can travel.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词变成一种模式的分类语，显示一个指广场的词能走多远。

intro.en: Both halves of marketplace are Latin borrowings, one for trade and one for a broad street, and the compound labels something older than either word.
intro.cn: marketplace 的两半都是拉丁借词，一半指交易，一半指宽阔的街；而这个复合词所标的事物比这两个词都古老。

items.en: Mercatus meant 'trade, traffic' and also 'a market', built on mercari 'to trade' and merx 'goods'. English market came from this noun through Germanic intermediaries.
items.cn: mercatus 意为「贸易、往来」，也指「市场」，建于 mercari「交易」与 merx「货物」之上。英语 market 经日耳曼语中介自这个名词而来。

items.en: Old English market is a borrowing from Latin mercatus, taken during the period of trade with the continent, so English has the Latin word twice, once directly and once through Germanic.
items.cn: 古英语 market 是从拉丁 mercatus 借来的，发生于与大陆贸易的时期；因此英语两次得到这个拉丁词，一次直接、一次经日耳曼语。

items.en: Place comes from Latin platea 'broad street', itself borrowed from Greek plateia (hodos) 'wide way', from platys 'broad'.
items.cn: place 来自拉丁 platea「宽阔的街」，而拉丁语又借自希腊 plateia (hodos)「宽路」，出自 platys「宽的」。

items.en: Old French place meant an open space or a square in a town, the sense English needs for the second half of the compound.
items.cn: 古法语 place 指城镇中的空地或广场，正是英语构成这个复合词后半所需之义。

items.en: Marketplace appears in English in the sixteenth century, when a town square with stalls needed a name distinct from market as an abstract trade.
items.cn: marketplace 于十六世纪出现在英语中，当时带摊位的城镇广场需要一个与抽象贸易义的 market 相区别的名称。

items.en: In the twenty-first century the compound is applied to online platforms, where no square exists but the same choosing among sellers takes place.
items.cn: 到二十一世纪，这个复合词被用于线上平台：那里没有广场，但同样的在卖家之间做挑选仍在上演。

note.en: The first group shares a half or a short form; the second holds words for places and systems of exchange.
note.cn: 第一组共享一半或一个短形式；第二组是交易场所与交易体系的其他说法。

entries.definition: The first element alone can mean trade in general, demand for a product, or a country region; only the compound insists on a physical square.
entries.definitionCN: 只取第一个成分时可泛指贸易、某产品的需求或某一国别市场；只有复合词才坚持指实体广场。

entries.definition: The second element alone means any location or a seat; it carries no trading sense by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 只取第二个成分时指任何地点或座位，本身不含交易义。

entries.definition: An old shortening of market, now mostly in names such as Wal-Mart or in historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: market 的旧缩略，今多用于沃尔玛这类名称或历史写作中。

entries.definition: The work of promoting goods, formed on market but naming an activity rather than a place.
entries.definitionCN: 推广货品的工作，由 market 构成，但指活动而非场所。

entries.definition: A market of many small stalls, often covered and in a region from North Africa to South Asia; it stresses the rows of shops.
entries.definitionCN: 由许多小摊构成的市场，常有顶棚，见于北非至南亚；强调成排的店铺。

entries.definition: An Arab market of narrow lanes, where each trade may occupy its own street.
entries.definitionCN: 阿拉伯世界由窄巷构成的市场，往往一种行业占一条街。

entries.definition: A market held at intervals, often with entertainment; the word stresses the occasion rather than the place.
entries.definitionCN: 定期举办、常带娱乐的市场；强调时机而非地点。

entries.definition: A formal venue or system for trading particular assets, such as a stock exchange; it has rules but no stalls.
entries.definitionCN: 交易特定资产的正式场所或体系，如证券交易所；有规则但无摊位。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: market 'trade' + place 'broad street': the street where trade happens.
normal.cn: market「交易」+ place「宽街」：交易发生的那条街。

normal.en: The family runs market, marketplace, marketing, marketer, marketable, supermarket, mart.
normal.cn: 同族词有 market、marketplace、marketing、marketer、marketable、supermarket、mart。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the widening: open-air marketplace, online marketplace, the marketplace of ideas.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出扩展：露天集市、线上市场、观念的市场。

normal.en: The compound needs a square; the short word does not: enter the market, but stand in the marketplace.
normal.cn: 复合词要求一块广场，短词不要求：进入市场，但站在集市里。

normal.en: The old law sense survives: a charter could grant a marketplace and its tolls.
normal.cn: 旧的法律义仍存：特许状可授予集市及随之的通行税。

abstract.en: Picture two rows of stalls with a narrow lane between them, and every choice made in that lane.
abstract.cn: 想象两排摊位之间一条窄道，所有选择都在这条窄道上做出。

abstract.en: Picture the same square rebuilt as a screen, with listings where cabbages used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象同一块广场被重建成一块屏幕，原来摆白菜的位置换成了商品页。

abstract.en: Picture a letters page where three historians bid for the same reader.
abstract.cn: 想象一个读者来信版，三位史家在那里争夺同一位读者。

examples.en: The marketplace empties by noon, when the ice under the fish has melted.
examples.cn: 到中午冰化成水，集市便空了。

examples.en: Small farmers sell through a marketplace that takes eight percent of every sale.
examples.cn: 小农通过一个抽取每笔交易百分之八的平台卖货。

examples.en: The university press put the book into a crowded marketplace with no advertising budget.
examples.cn: 这家大学出版社把书投进一个拥挤的市场，却没有广告预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: market（买卖）+ place（地方）＝ 买卖发生的那块地；先想露天的棚，再想屏幕里的货架。

root: market 来自拉丁 mercatus「贸易、市场」（经日耳曼语进入古英语）；place 来自拉丁 platea「宽阔的街」，再溯至希腊 plateia hodos「宽路」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a square to a business model: the open stalls, the arena of competition, the online platform, the single-trade hall, the demand to be found, the charter right, the arena of argument, and the platform classifier.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一块广场走到一种商业模式：露天摊位、竞争场域、线上平台、单一行业场所、可被找到的需求、特许权、论辩场域，以及平台分类语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rows of stalls with a lane between them, and a buyer walking that lane twice before choosing.
core.cn: 核心意象：两排摊位之间一条窄道，买主在那条道上走两遍才决定。

branches.en: A SQUARE AND A SPECIALITY: the general open market, then one commodity claiming a hall of its own.
branches.cn: 广场与专营：先是综合的露天市场，再是一种货品占据自己的场馆。

branches.en: MARKET AS ARENA: competition and demand are the square made abstract enough to enter and leave.
branches.cn: 作为场域的市场：竞争与需求就是被抽象到可以进出的一块广场。

branches.en: SOFTWARE AND MODEL: the platform rebuilds the stalls and then becomes a way of doing business.
branches.cn: 软件与模式：平台重建了摊位，随后本身成了一种做生意的方式。

branches.en: A RIGHT BEFORE A PLACE: a charter can create the market by granting it.
branches.cn: 先有权利后有地点：特许状可以靠授予来造出集市。

branches.en: BUYERS OF ARGUMENTS: ideas are weighed by readers the way goods are weighed by shoppers.
branches.cn: 论点的买主：观念被读者权衡，正如货物被顾客权衡。

intro.en: Marketplace is two borrowed nouns compounded, and each half has produced a family of its own in English.
intro.cn: marketplace 是两个借来的名词复合而成，每一半在英语里都各自衍生出一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin mercatus 'trade, market' supplies market, marketing and marketable; Latin platea 'broad street' supplies place, replace and placement. Greek plateia stands behind platea.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mercatus「交易、市场」给出 market、marketing、marketable；拉丁 platea「宽街」给出 place、replace、placement。希腊 plateia 是 platea 的来源。

items.example: The first element can stand alone as noun or verb.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分可独立作名词或动词。

items.example: The second element supplies the ground.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分提供那块地面。

items.example: The element recurs in workplace and showplace.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分在 workplace 与 showplace 中重现。

items.example: The compound fixes the abstract word to ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把抽象的词固定在地面上。

items.example: The suffix turns a place into an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把场所变成活动。

items.example: The person form follows the usual agent pattern.
items.exampleCN: 人称形式遵循常见的施动模式。

items.example: The suffix marks what a market will accept.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出市场会接受什么。

items.example: The prefix raises the scale of the square.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀抬高了广场的规模。

items.example: The place root also builds verbs of position.
items.exampleCN: place 词根也构成表位置的动词。

items.example: The clipping survives in trade names.
items.exampleCN: 这一缩略形式留存于商号名称中。
