definition_zh: 交换；兑换；（证券交易所等）交易场所；短暂交谈；交换所
definition_en: the act of giving one thing and receiving another in its place
core_image: 两手同时伸出，各自把东西递到对方掌心，收回时已换了一样
scene: 车站门口，两个旅客把各自的车票递过去，看对方的座位是否更靠窗。They agreed to an exchange of seats so the child could sit by the window.
sceneCN: 这里 exchange 指「两方互给互取的交换」（第 1 个义项：作为一次对等交换）；句意为他们同意换座位，好让孩子靠窗坐。

pos.zh: 交换；兑换；交易场所；短暂交谈
交换；兑换

derivatives.zh: exchange + -able（可…的）→ 可交换的；可兑换的
inter-（相互）+ change → 互换；换乘站
interchange + -able → 可互换的
拉丁 cambiare（交换）经古法语 → 改变；零钱（同根，语义分叉为「变」）
bureau + de + change → 外币兑换处（法语借入）
exchange + -er → 交换器（如热交换器）

senses.title: Giving one thing for another
senses.definition: the act of giving something and receiving something else in return
senses.definitionCN: 给出某物并换回另一物的行为
senses.example: They agreed to an exchange of seats so the child could sit by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他们同意换座位，好让孩子靠窗坐。
senses.why: Latin ex- 'out' plus cambiare 'to barter' gives a giving out that is answered by a taking in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 ex-「出」加 cambiare「以物易物」，给出一个「给出」并由「取回」回应的动作。

senses.title: A venue for trading securities or currencies
senses.titleCN: 证券或货币的交易场所
senses.definition: an organized market where financial instruments or currencies are bought and sold
senses.definitionCN: 买卖金融工具或货币的有组织市场
senses.example: The exchange closed early when the storm cut the power.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨切断电力，交易所提前收盘。
senses.why: A place where values are exchanged takes the name of the act, and the act becomes a building.
senses.whyCN: 交换价值的地方取了动作之名，动作也就成了一座建筑。

senses.title: An exchange of letters or remarks
senses.definition: a series of communications between two parties, as an exchange of letters or views
senses.definitionCN: 两方之间一系列的书信或意见往来
senses.example: The exchange of letters lasted three years and settled nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 书信往来进行三年，什么也没解决。
senses.why: Words are given and words are returned, so correspondence is the same shape as trade.
senses.whyCN: 话被给出，话又被送回，因此通信与交易是同一个形状。

senses.title: A short argument or conversation
senses.definition: a brief, often heated, passage of talk between two people
senses.definitionCN: 两人之间一段简短、常带火气的对话
senses.example: A sharp exchange at the door ended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 门口一场尖锐的交锋结束了这次会面。
senses.why: The countable sense shrinks a whole correspondence into one round of give and take.
senses.whyCN: 可数义把整段往来缩小为一个给出与回敬的回合。

senses.title: A telephone switchboard
senses.definition: dated technical: a building or apparatus where lines are connected by an operator
senses.definitionCN: 旧技术用语：由话务员接通线路的机房或设备
senses.example: The old exchange on the corner still has a manual board.
senses.exampleCN: 街角那间旧交换机房仍有一台人工交换台。
senses.why: Lines are exchanged between callers, and the machinery that performs the exchange takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 线路在通话者之间被交换，执行交换的机器便取了这个名字。

senses.title: A swap of captives or personnel
senses.definition: an agreed handing over of prisoners, spies or personnel by two sides
senses.definitionCN: 两方商定的战俘、间谍或人员交还
senses.example: The prisoner exchange took place at a border bridge at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 战俘交换在黎明时分的一座边境桥上进行。
senses.why: People are treated as the things given and received, which is why the plain word is used without euphemism.
senses.whyCN: 人被当作被给出与接收的对象，因此这里直用这个普通的词，不加委婉语。

senses.title: To swap (verb)
senses.definition: to give something and receive something else in return, or to give each other
senses.definitionCN: 给出某物并换回另一物，或互相给予
senses.example: The two schools exchange students every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这两所学校每年春天交换学生。
senses.why: The verb makes the noun into a repeated or mutual act.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个名词变成反复或相互的动作。

senses.title: Conversion of one currency for another
senses.definition: the changing of money of one country into that of another at a stated rate
senses.definitionCN: 按既定比价把一国货币换为另一国货币
senses.example: The exchange cost him nine percent before he left the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 他还没出机场，兑换就花掉了他百分之九。
senses.why: A money counter is the same gesture with one currency on each side, so no separate word is needed.
senses.whyCN: 换钱的柜台是同一个动作，只是两侧各放一种货币，因此无需另造新词。

senses.title: An organized programme of visits
senses.definition: a scheme in which people from two places visit each other, as a student or cultural exchange
senses.definitionCN: 两地人员互访的安排，如学生交流或文化交流
senses.example: The cultural exchange brought twelve potters to the city for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这项文化交流把十二位陶工请到城里住了一个月。
senses.why: An institution borrows the word for reciprocal visits, since each side hosts and is hosted.
senses.whyCN: 一种制度借用了这个词来指互访，因为每一方既接待也被接待。

intro.en: Exchange is a French-shaped verb from spoken Latin, and its key root is one of the least certain in this batch.
intro.cn: exchange 是一个由口语拉丁而来、带法语形态的动词，其核心词根是本批中最不确定的几个之一。

items.en: Cambiare meant 'to exchange, to barter'. Its own origin is uncertain: a link to a Celtic verb for 'change' is often suggested, but no derivation has been demonstrated.
items.cn: cambiare 意为「交换、以物易物」。它自身的来源不确定：常有人提出它与某个凯尔特语表「改变」的动词有关，但没有任何派生得到证实。

items.en: Spoken Latin added ex- 'out' to cambiare, producing *excambiare 'to exchange out, to swap'.
items.cn: 口语拉丁给 cambiare 加上 ex-「出」，构成 *excambiare「换出、交换」。

items.en: Old French eschangier continues the spoken form and supplies the -ch- that English preserves in the noun.
items.cn: 古法语 eschangier 承接口语形式，并提供英语名词中保留的那个 -ch-。

items.en: English borrows the word in the fourteenth century as both noun and verb, first for swapping goods and then for money changing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪把这个词作为名词与动词一并借入，先指换货，后指换钱。

items.en: The financial sense develops with the rise of the bourse: a place where bills and currencies are exchanged becomes simply the exchange.
items.cn: 金融义随交易所的兴起而发展：买卖票据与货币的场所干脆就被称作 the exchange。

items.en: The telephone exchange extends the word to a room where lines are connected, a sense now largely historical.
items.cn: 电话交换机把这个词扩展到接通线路的机房，这一义项如今大体已成历史。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the shape and is easily confused; the second holds words for swaps and for trading venues.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根或外形，容易混淆；第二组是交换行为与交易场所的其他说法。

entries.definition: The short form of the same Latin root, but it means to become different as well as to swap; exchange keeps only the two-way giving.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词根的短形式，但除交换外还指「变得不同」；exchange 只保留双向给予之义。

entries.definition: Inter- 'between' plus change marks a two-way swap, and in transport it names a junction where routes swap passengers.
entries.definitionCN: inter-「之间」加 change 标出双向互换，在交通中指路线互换乘客的枢纽。

entries.definition: The adjective means able to be swapped or converted, often in economics or law rather than in daily speech.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词指可交换或可兑换，多见于经济或法律语境而非日常口语。

entries.definition: A tax on goods, from a different Latin source (ex- plus caedere 'to cut'); it has nothing to do with swapping.
entries.definitionCN: 指货物税，来自另一个拉丁来源（ex- 加 caedere「切」），与交换无关。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a mutual exchange, usually of similar things and often without paperwork.
entries.definitionCN: 互相交换的日常用词，通常换同类之物，且常无手续。

entries.definition: An exchange carried on as business, especially of goods; exchange is neutral about whether money is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 作为生意的交换，尤指货物；exchange 不限定是否涉及钱。

entries.definition: Exchange with no money at all; it is one strict kind of exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 完全不用钱的交换，是 exchange 的一个严格子类。

entries.definition: Changing one thing into another form, often without a second party; exchange requires someone on the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 把一物变为另一形式，常无第二方；exchange 则要求对面有人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + cambiare 'barter': hand something out and take something in.
normal.cn: ex-「出」+ cambiare「以物易物」：把东西递出去，再收一件回来。

normal.en: The family runs exchange, exchangeable, interchange, interchangeable, changer, change.
normal.cn: 同族词有 exchange、exchangeable、interchange、interchangeable、changer、change。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the venues: stock exchange, exchange rate, labour exchange, telephone exchange.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出场所：证券交易所、汇率、职业介绍所、电话交换机。

normal.en: The verb is mutual: two schools exchange students, and each is host and guest.
normal.cn: 动词是相互的：两校交换学生，各自既是主人也是客人。

normal.en: Words exchange too: an exchange of views is correspondence with the same shape.
normal.cn: 话也能交换：交换意见就是同形状的往来。

abstract.en: Picture two palms opening at the same moment, each now holding what the other had.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手掌同时张开，各自握着对方原来拿的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a building with no goods in it, only numbers being swapped all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一座里面没有货物、整天只在交换数字的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture an operator plugging a line into a socket so two strangers can talk.
abstract.cn: 想象话务员把一根线插进插孔，好让两个陌生人通话。

examples.en: The two museums arranged an exchange of paintings for a season.
examples.cn: 两家博物馆安排了一季的绘画互换。

examples.en: He exchanged his seat for a place by the aisle and slept the whole way.
examples.cn: 他换到靠过道的座位，一路睡了过去。

examples.en: The exchange rate moved two percent before the markets opened.
examples.cn: 开市之前，汇率已经动了两成中的两个百分点。

dict_mnemonic.text: ex（出）+ change（换）＝ 把东西换出去，换回一样；先记「两只手同时递」，再记「一所房子专门换数字」。

root: 拉丁 cambiare「交换、以物易物」+ ex-「出」→ 口语拉丁 *excambiare → 古法语 eschangier → 英语 exchange；cambiare 来源不确定，与凯尔特语的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one gesture of give and take: a swap, a hall of swaps, words swapped, one sharp round of words, a switchboard, captives handed over, the verb, currency conversion, and a programme of mutual visits.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一个「递出与接回」的动作展开：一次交换、专门交换的场所、交换话语、一个尖锐的话语回合、交换机、交出俘虏、动词、货币兑换，以及互访项目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands opening at once, each receiving exactly what the other releases.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手同时张开，各自接到的正是对方松开的。

branches.en: THE GESTURE AND THE VERB: one completed swap, then the same act performed habitually or mutually.
branches.cn: 动作与动词：一次完成的交换，再是同一动作被反复或相互地做。

branches.en: PLACES AND MACHINES OF SWAPPING: a hall for securities, a room for telephone lines, a counter for currencies.
branches.cn: 交换的场所与机器：换证券的大厅、接线路的机房、换货币的柜台。

branches.en: WORDS IN PLACE OF GOODS: correspondence over years, or one sharp round at a door.
branches.cn: 以话代货：经年的通信，或门口一个尖锐的回合。

branches.en: PEOPLE HANDED OVER: the plain word is used without euphemism for prisoners.
branches.cn: 被交出的人：对俘虏直接用这个普通的词，不加委婉。

branches.en: AN INSTITUTION OF HOSTING: each side gives a visit and receives one, so a programme becomes an exchange.
branches.cn: 接待的制度：每一方给出一次访问也收到一次，于是项目本身成了 exchange。

intro.en: Exchange is one Latin prefix plus one uncertain Latin verb, and both parts recur in English words about movement and substitution.
intro.cn: exchange 是一个拉丁前缀加一个来源不确定的拉丁动词，两部分在英语中反复出现于表移动与替代的词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin cambiare 'to barter' gives change, exchange, interchange and the money-changing phrases; ex- 'out' recurs in exit, export and extract. The root behind cambiare is not established.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cambiare「以物易物」给出 change、exchange、interchange 与换钱的短语；ex-「出」在 exit、export、extract 中重现。cambiare 之后的词根未得到证实。

items.example: The prefix marks something handed out.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出被递出去的东西。

items.example: The verb's own origin is uncertain.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词自身的来源不确定。

items.example: The compound is both noun and verb in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词在英语中兼作名词与动词。

items.example: The short form widened to mean alteration.
items.exampleCN: 这个短形式扩大为指「改变」。

items.example: The suffix makes a legal or economic property.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出法律或经济属性。

items.example: The prefix adds two directions.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀添上两个方向。

items.example: The double suffix marks substitutability.
items.exampleCN: 双层后缀标出可替代性。

items.example: The agent suffix is common in engineering.
items.exampleCN: 这个施动后缀在工程用语中常见。

items.example: The phrase keeps the French noun unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语保留法语名词原形。

definition_zh: 以货易货；物物交换；（比喻）以某物换取他物；旧义：讨价还价
definition_en: to trade goods or services by exchanging them directly, without using money
core_image: 两户人家在院门口各提一篮东西，一篮鸡蛋换一篮盐，谁也不掏钱
scene: 山村里没有现钱，村民提着一篮鸡蛋走到邻家门口，换回一小袋盐。In the hill villages people still barter eggs for salt.
sceneCN: 这里 barter 指「不用钱、直接以货换货」（第 3 个义项：作为动词的物物交换）；句意为山村里的人至今仍用鸡蛋换盐。

pos.zh: 物物交换；以货易货（不可数）
以货易货；交换

derivatives.zh: barter + -er（从事者）→ 以货易货的人
barter + -ing（动名词）→ 易货行为
barter + -ed（被动分词）→ 以货换来的
barter + economy → 易货经济（人类学术语）
counter-（对应）+ trade → 对销贸易（现代对应概念，非同根）
古法语 troquer（交换）→ 以物易物（旧义，同义不同源）

senses.title: Exchange of goods without money
senses.definition: the practice of trading goods or services by direct exchange, with no currency involved
senses.definitionCN: 以直接交换的方式买卖货物或服务，不使用货币的做法
senses.example: In the hill villages people still barter eggs for salt.
senses.exampleCN: 山村里的人至今仍用鸡蛋换盐。
senses.why: The word came into English meaning to cheat and then to deal, and the money-free exchange is the sense that settled.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语时意为「欺骗」，随后转为「交易」，最终定型的是不用钱的交换义。

senses.title: One such transaction
senses.definition: a single deal in which one lot of goods is handed over for another
senses.definitionCN: 以一批货物换另一批货物的单笔交易
senses.example: The barter was settled in an hour: three sacks of grain for one ewe.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔易货一小时内就谈定：三袋谷子换一只母羊。
senses.why: The mass noun can be counted when a particular deal is meant, as with most trade words.
senses.whyCN: 与多数贸易词一样，这个不可数名词在指某笔具体交易时可以计件。

senses.title: To exchange goods as a verb
senses.definition: to give goods or services in return for other goods or services rather than for money
senses.definitionCN: 以货物或服务换取其他货物或服务，而非换取货币
senses.example: The clinic barters dental work for carpentry.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所拿牙科治疗换木工活。
senses.why: The verb takes the practice and makes it an act that two parties perform on each other.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这一做法变成两方对彼此实施的动作。

senses.title: To give something away at a loss
senses.definition: figuratively, to surrender something valuable in return for much less, as to barter away a right
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指以远低于价值的东西换出珍贵之物，如断送一项权利
senses.example: The ministry bartered away its independence for a year of funding.
senses.exampleCN: 该部门为了一年的经费断送了独立性。
senses.why: If goods can be traded, anything can be traded badly, and the particle away marks the loss.
senses.whyCN: 既然货物可以交换，任何东西都可以换得很糟，而副词 away 标出这种损失。

senses.title: An economy built on such exchange
senses.definition: a system in which goods are exchanged directly because money is absent, scarce or untrusted
senses.definitionCN: 因货币缺失、稀缺或不受信任而直接交换货物的体系
senses.example: A barter economy returns whenever the currency collapses.
senses.exampleCN: 只要货币崩溃，易货经济就会回来。
senses.why: Anthropology and economics turned the practice into a named system, often as a contrast to money.
senses.whyCN: 人类学与经济学把这一做法变成有名目的体系，常作为货币的对立面。

senses.title: A business deal paid in kind
senses.titleCN: 以实物或服务支付的企业交易
senses.definition: a commercial arrangement in which goods or services are paid for with other goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 以货物或服务支付货物或服务的商业安排
senses.example: The airline barters seats for hotel rooms in the off-season.
senses.exampleCN: 淡季时这家航空公司用座位换酒店房间。
senses.why: Firms with unsold stock prefer to swap it rather than write it off, so the old word returns to business.
senses.whyCN: 有滞销存货的企业宁愿换掉也不愿核销，于是这个老词回到商业中。

senses.title: A political swap of support
senses.definition: an informal arrangement in which votes or favours are exchanged for other votes or favours
senses.definitionCN: 以选票或人情换取其他选票或人情的非正式安排
senses.example: The two blocs bartered votes on the transport bill.
senses.exampleCN: 两个集团在交通法案上交换了选票。
senses.why: Where money cannot legally pass, support itself becomes the currency.
senses.whyCN: 在钱不能合法流通的地方，支持本身就变成了通货。

senses.title: To haggle over a price, in older use
senses.definition: archaic: to argue over terms, to chaffer or haggle, a sense closer to the word's original French meaning
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法：为条件争执、讨价还价，这一义项更接近其法语原义
senses.example: In the old play the farmers barter for an hour before they agree.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部旧剧里，农人们讨价还价一个钟头才谈成。
senses.why: Old French barater meant to deceive and to chaffer, and haggling survives as the residue of that sense.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 barater 意为欺骗与讨价，讨价还价义就是那一层的残留。

intro.en: Barter is one of the few words in this batch whose origin no one can settle, and its history begins with cheating rather than with fair dealing.
intro.cn: barter 是本批中少数来源无人能定的词之一，而它的历史以欺骗、而非公平交易开始。

items.en: Barater meant 'to deceive, to cheat', and only later 'to exchange or chaffer'. Its own origin is uncertain, and suggestions of a Celtic or imitative source remain hypotheses.
items.cn: barater 意为「欺骗、欺诈」，后来才有「交换、讨价」之义。它自身的来源不确定，指向凯尔特语或拟声来源的说法仍属假说。

items.en: No source for Old French barater can be demonstrated. The word may be regional slang that spread, but that too is a hypothesis rather than a finding.
items.cn: 古法语 barater 的来源无法证实。它可能是扩散开来的地方俚语，但这也只是假说，而非研究结论。

items.en: English takes the verb in the fifteenth century, still with a smell of cheating about it, as in to barter away.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪接来这个动词，仍带着欺骗的意味，如 barter away 的用法。

items.en: By the sixteenth century barter settles into 'to trade by exchange of goods', the sense that has survived, while the cheating sense fades.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，barter 落定为「以交换货物做买卖」，这一义项留存下来，而欺骗义淡出。

items.en: Economists and anthropologists make barter economy and barter system into technical terms, usually as the imagined opposite of money.
items.cn: 经济学家与人类学家把易货经济、易货体系变成术语，通常把它当作货币的想象对立面。

items.en: Twentieth-century business revives the word for in-kind deals between firms, and barter away survives as the moral warning attached to it.
items.cn: 二十世纪商业让这个词在企业间的实物交易中复活，而 barter away 作为附在其上的道德警告留存下来。

note.en: The first group is a set of look-alikes, one of them a false friend; the second holds words for exchange and for haggling.
note.cn: 第一组是一组形近词，其中一个为假朋友；第二组是交换与讨价的其他说法。

entries.definition: A fence or obstacle, from Old French barriere; it shares the shape but not the root or the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 围栏或障碍，来自古法语 barriere；外形相同，但词根与词义都不同。

entries.definition: To hit repeatedly, from a different origin; nothing is exchanged and nothing is traded.
entries.definitionCN: 反复击打，来源不同；既不交换也不交易。

entries.definition: A person who serves drinks behind a bar; the first element is bar, a counter, and the second is tender.
entries.definitionCN: 在吧台后上酒的人；前一成分是 bar（柜台），后一成分是 tender。

entries.definition: The person who barters, formed properly with the agent suffix; it is the word the false friends imitate.
entries.definitionCN: 以货易货的人，按施动后缀正确构成；形近词模仿的正是这一形式。

entries.definition: Any buying and selling, with or without money; barter is the money-free subset.
entries.definitionCN: 任何买卖，含钱或不含钱；barter 是不用钱的子集。

entries.definition: To exchange two things, often one for one and often casually; barter adds the commercial, no-money frame.
entries.definitionCN: 交换两样东西，常一对一且较随意；barter 另带商业性的不用钱框架。

entries.definition: In old use, to truck meant to barter or deal; the modern vehicle sense is a different word with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 旧用法中 to truck 指以货易货或交易；现代「卡车」义是另一个来源不同的词。

entries.definition: To argue about a price; it names the talk around a deal, whereas barter names the deal itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为价格争执；它指交易周围的谈话，而 barter 指交易本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: No coin appears anywhere in the sense: eggs go out, salt comes in.
normal.cn: 这个义项里没有一枚硬币：鸡蛋出去，盐进来。

normal.en: The family runs barter, barterer, bartering, bartered, barter economy, barter deal.
normal.cn: 同族词有 barter、barterer、bartering、bartered、barter economy、barter deal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the system: barter system, barter trade, barter away.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出体系：物物交换体系、易货贸易、断送。

normal.en: The verb is older than the honest sense: barater first meant to cheat.
normal.cn: 动词比诚实义更老：barater 最初意为欺骗。

normal.en: Barter away is the moral form: what is swapped may be a right, not a good.
normal.cn: barter away 是道德形态：被换掉的可能是权利，而非货物。

abstract.en: Picture two doorways facing each other, each with a basket set down and picked up.
abstract.cn: 想象两个相对的门口，各自放下又提起一只篮子。

abstract.en: Picture a market where every price tag is blank because nothing has a money value.
abstract.cn: 想象一个所有价签都空白的市场，因为没有任何东西有货币价格。

abstract.en: Picture a clinic where a filling is paid for with a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一间诊所，补一颗牙用一个架子来付账。

examples.en: Before the currency reform, factories bartered steel for electricity.
examples.cn: 货币改革之前，工厂用钢材换电。

examples.en: She bartered two hours of translation for a repaired bicycle.
examples.cn: 她用两小时翻译换了一辆修好的自行车。

examples.en: The report warns that the country is bartering away its forests for short-term loans.
examples.cn: 报告警告说，这个国家正用森林换取短期贷款。

dict_mnemonic.text: barter＝一手交蛋、一手交盐；记住「没有钱的声音」，只有一个递出、一个接住。

root: 古法语 barater「欺骗、欺诈」，后转为「交换、讨价」；其自身来源不确定，凯尔特语或拟声来源的说法均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one deal in view: the money-free practice, one such deal, the verb, the loss-making version, the named economy, the corporate deal, the political swap, and the old sense of haggling.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项始终盯着同一笔交易：不用钱的做法、一笔具体交易、动词、亏本的换出、有名目的经济、企业交易、政治交换，以及旧的讨价义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two baskets set down at the same moment, and no coin anywhere between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只篮子同时放下，两者之间没有一枚硬币。

chain: EACH NEEDS WHAT THE OTHER HAS

branches.en: PRACTICE AND INSTANCE: the general money-free habit, then one basket for one basket.
branches.cn: 做法与个例：不用钱的通则，再是一篮换一篮。

branches.en: VERB AND FIRM: what villagers do, companies also do with unsold stock and empty rooms.
branches.cn: 动词与企业：村民做的事，企业也拿滞销存货与空房间来做。

branches.en: THE BAD SWAP: anything can be bartered away, including rights and forests.
branches.cn: 糟糕的交换：任何东西都能被换掉，包括权利与森林。

branches.en: A NAMED SYSTEM: economists turn the habit into a stage or an alternative to money.
branches.cn: 有名目的体系：经济学家把这一习惯变成一个阶段或货币的替代。

branches.en: CURRENCY WITHOUT MONEY: votes and terms become what is traded, and haggling is the talk around it.
branches.cn: 无货币的通货：选票与条件成了被交换之物，而讨价是其周围的谈话。

intro.en: Barter is a bare borrowed verb that takes ordinary English endings, and the compounds below show it moving from villages to boardrooms.
intro.cn: barter 是一个光秃秃的借来动词，只接普通的英语词尾，下面的复合词显示它从村庄走进董事会。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source behind barter: it comes through Old French from a word whose origin is uncertain, and its endings are plain English. The revived synonym truck came from a different French verb.
latinIntro.cn: barter 背后没有拉丁来源：它经古法语自一个来源不确定的词而来，词尾都是普通英语。复活起来的同义词 truck 来自另一个法语动词。

items.example: The bare stem works as noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干兼作名词与动词。

items.example: The suffix gives barterer, not the look-alike bartender.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出 barterer，而不是形近的 bartender。

items.example: Bartering names the ongoing practice.
items.exampleCN: bartering 指持续进行的做法。

items.example: The participle serves as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词可作形容词。

items.example: The compound turns a habit into an institution.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把习惯变成制度。

items.example: The compound counts a single case.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指单笔事例。

items.example: The phrase is standard in anthropology.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语是人类学的标准说法。

items.example: The particle carries the sense of loss.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词带出损失之义。

items.meaningCN: 国家间的现代对销贸易
items.example: The modern term replaces barter in treaties.
items.exampleCN: 现代条约用语以它替代 barter。

definition_zh: 铸币；硬币制度；新造的词（或新造之物）；铸币权
definition_en: the system of coins used in a country, the act of making them, or a newly invented word
core_image: 一枚银片夹在两块模具之间，锤子落下，花纹从边缘挤进银面
scene: 作坊里，工匠把一枚银片放在两片模具之间，用锤子砸下，边缘的花纹陷进银面。The coinage of the realm changed when the old die wore out.
sceneCN: 这里 coinage 指「一国所使用的硬币体系」（第 1 个义项：作为整套流通硬币）；句意为旧模具磨损之后，这个王国的铸币体系随之改变。

pos.zh: 铸币；硬币体系；新造词（不可数，或作可数指一种币制）

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 cuneus（楔子）经古法语 coin（模具）→ 硬币；铸造；造词
coin + -er（从事者）→ 铸币者；造词者（语义偏移：从工人转到造词人）
coin + -ing（动名词）→ 铸造；造词行为
coin + operated → 投币式的（语义偏移：从货币转到机械）
mint + -age（同型后缀，不同词干）→ 铸造量；铸币费
neo-（新）+ logos（词）→ 新词（同义不同源）

senses.title: The coins of a country as a system
senses.titleCN: 一国硬币构成的整套体系
senses.definition: the set of coins in use in a country, considered as one system with fixed denominations
senses.definitionCN: 一国流通中按固定面额组成的整套硬币
senses.example: The coinage of the realm changed when the old die wore out.
senses.exampleCN: 旧模具磨损之后，这个王国的铸币体系随之改变。
senses.why: The Latin word for a wedge named the die that stamped metal, and the product took the name of the tool.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表「楔子」的词指冲压金属的模具，产物便继承了工具之名。

senses.title: The act or process of minting
senses.definition: the work of cutting dies and striking blanks into legal coins
senses.definitionCN: 刻制模具并把坯饼冲压成法定硬币的工作
senses.example: Coinage was moved to the capital so the dies could be guarded.
senses.exampleCN: 铸币工序迁到首都，以便看守模具。
senses.why: The suffix -age names an action or its product, so the same noun covers the making and the made.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -age 既指动作也指产物，因此同一个名词兼指制造与制成品。

senses.title: A newly invented word
senses.definition: a word or phrase invented rather than inherited, often to name something new
senses.definitionCN: 非继承而来、通常为命名新事物而造出的词或短语
senses.example: The verb is a coinage of the nineteen-twenties, not an old farming word.
senses.exampleCN: 这个动词是二十世纪二十年代的新造词，并非古老的农事词。
senses.why: Striking a new piece of metal and striking a new word are the same gesture: something new is impressed with a known stamp.
senses.whyCN: 冲压一枚新币与造一个新词是同一动作：新东西被打上已知的印记。

senses.title: The act of inventing a word
senses.definition: the deliberate invention of vocabulary by a writer, a trade or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 由作者、行业或机构刻意创造词汇的行为
senses.example: His coinage of the term was mocked for a decade and then adopted everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 他造的这个术语被嘲笑了十年，然后到处被采用。
senses.why: The countable act sense follows from the product sense, as with other -age nouns.
senses.whyCN: 可数的行为义由产物义引出，与其他 -age 名词一样。

senses.title: The right to strike coins
senses.definition: historical: the sovereign right to issue coin, often granted or leased to a mint
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法：发行硬币的君主权，常授予或租给造币厂
senses.example: The city held coinage rights for two centuries and grew rich on the fee.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市握有铸币权两个世纪，靠这项费用致富。
senses.why: A right over the tool becomes a right over the word, and coinage comes to mean the privilege itself.
senses.whyCN: 对工具的权利变成对词的权利，coinage 于是指这项特权本身。

senses.title: The quantity of coins issued
senses.definition: the amount of coin struck in a period, or one issue of a particular denomination
senses.definitionCN: 某时期铸造的硬币数量，或某一面额的某次发行
senses.example: The silver coinage of that year was recalled within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年的银币在十年之内就被收回了。
senses.why: An uncountable product noun can be counted when a single issue or batch is meant.
senses.whyCN: 不可数的产物名词在指单次发行或单批时可以被计数。

senses.title: Something invented that passes as real
senses.definition: figuratively, a fabricated thing that circulates as if it were genuine, such as a coinage of propaganda
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指当作真物流传的编造之物，如宣传中造出的说法
senses.example: The phrase was a coinage of the ministry, repeated until it sounded like a fact.
senses.exampleCN: 这个说法是该部造出来的，被反复引用，直到听起来像事实。
senses.why: Counterfeit coin and counterfeit word share the idea of a stamp without the metal behind it.
senses.whyCN: 伪币与伪词共享同一观念：印记有了，背后却没有金属。

senses.title: A coined name for a product or place
senses.titleCN: 为产品或地方造出的名称
senses.definition: a commercial or official name invented for marketing rather than grown from the language
senses.definitionCN: 为营销或官方用途造出、而非从语言中自然长出的名称
senses.example: The brand is a coinage, built to be pronounceable in twelve languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌名是造出来的，为的是在十二种语言里都能念。
senses.why: Naming is the most commercial form of coining: a word is struck to circulate like a coin.
senses.whyCN: 命名是造词最商业化的形式：词被冲压出来，像硬币一样流通。

intro.en: Coinage begins with a wedge of metal, passes through a French word for the die, and ends up naming both money and new words.
intro.cn: coinage 从一块楔形金属开始，经过一个指模具的法语词，最后同时命名货币与新词。

items.en: Cuneus meant 'wedge'. The die that struck ancient coins was a wedge-shaped block, so the tool's name became the name of the thing struck.
items.cn: cuneus 意为「楔子」。冲压古币的模具是一块楔形物，于是工具之名成了被冲压之物的名字。

items.en: Old French coin meant 'die, stamp' and also 'corner, wedge'; English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 coin 指「模具、印戳」，也指「角、楔」；英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: English first uses coin for the die and then for the piece of money, with the verb to coin following immediately.
items.cn: 英语先用 coin 指模具，随后指钱币，动词「铸造」随即跟上。

items.en: Moneta, the title of Juno whose temple housed the Roman mint, gives money and monetary by a separate route; it is not the source of coin.
items.cn: Moneta 是朱诺的称号，她的神庙设有罗马造币厂，经另一条路径给出 money 与 monetary；它不是 coin 的来源。

items.en: Coin plus the French suffix -age produces coinage, first for the act of minting and then for the coins themselves.
items.cn: coin 加法语后缀 -age 构成 coinage，先指铸造行为，再指硬币本身。

items.en: The word sense develops in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, when writers begin to speak of coining new terms as striking new pieces.
items.cn: 造词义在十六、十七世纪发展出来，当时写作者开始把造新术语说成冲压新币。

note.en: The first group is built on coin and its tool; the second holds words for money systems and for invented vocabulary.
note.cn: 第一组建于 coin 及其工具之上；第二组是货币体系与生造词汇的说法。

entries.definition: A single piece of money, or the act of striking one; coinage is the system, the process or the new word.
entries.definitionCN: 一枚钱币，或冲压它的动作；coinage 则是体系、过程或新词。

entries.definition: One who mints or one who invents words; the agent form of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 铸币者或造词者；同一词干的施动形式。

entries.definition: Built like coinage but on mint: it means the quantity struck or the charge for striking.
entries.definitionCN: 与 coinage 同型但建于 mint：指铸造量或铸造费。

entries.definition: A compound for machines that take a coin; the word here is the object, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 指投币机器的复合词；此处指物件，而非体系。

entries.definition: All money in use in a country, notes as well as coin; coinage covers only the metal part or the system behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 一国流通的全部货币，含纸币与硬币；coinage 只涵盖金属部分或其背后的体系。

entries.definition: The technical process of making coins; coinage also means the resulting system or the right to issue.
entries.definitionCN: 制币的技术过程；coinage 另指由此形成的体系或发行权。

entries.definition: The learned word for a new expression; coinage is the looser, more image-bearing term for the same thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指新表达的学术用词；coinage 是同一事物的更松散、更带比喻的说法。

entries.definition: Money a creditor must accept; it describes legal force, while coinage describes the stock of metal pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 债权人必须接受的货币；它描述法律效力，而 coinage 描述金属币的存量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: coin 'die' + -age 'process or product': the stamping and what it stamps out.
normal.cn: coin「模具」+ -age「过程或产物」：冲压的动作与被冲压出来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs coin, coinage, coiner, coining, coin-operated, and the parallel mintage.
normal.cn: 同族词有 coin、coinage、coiner、coining、coin-operated，以及同型的 mintage。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: decimal coinage, coinage rights, a new coinage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：十进制币制、铸币权、一个新造词。

normal.en: Money and words share the verb: you coin a phrase the way a mint coins a piece.
normal.cn: 钱与词共享同一个动词：你造一个短语，正如造币厂冲压一枚硬币。

normal.en: The word for the die survived inside the word for the money.
normal.cn: 指模具的词留在了指货币的词里面。

abstract.en: Picture a wedge-shaped die coming down on a blank and leaving a face where there was none.
abstract.cn: 想象一块楔形模具落在空白坯饼上，留下原本没有的一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a phrase repeated by a ministry until listeners forget it was invented.
abstract.cn: 想象一个由某个部门反复使用的说法，直到听者忘了它是造出来的。

abstract.en: Picture a brand name tested in twelve languages before anyone hears it as a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个品牌名在十二种语言里先试过，才被当作词听见。

examples.en: The colony had no coinage of its own and used whatever foreign silver arrived.
examples.cn: 这块殖民地没有自己的币制，有什么外国银币来就用什么。

examples.en: The word is a coinage of the nineteenth century, not a native term.
examples.cn: 这个词是十九世纪的新造词，不是本族语词。

examples.en: Coinage rights were leased to a family bank for a hundred years.
examples.cn: 铸币权被租给一家家族银行一百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: coin（模具、硬币）+ age（过程）＝ 打币这件事和打出来的币；再造个词，也是同一个动作。

root: 拉丁 cuneus「楔子」（模具为楔形）→ 古法语 coin「模具、印戳」→ 英语 coin「硬币；铸造」+ -age → coinage；与拉丁 moneta（造币厂）为不同来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from one struck blank to one invented word: the coin system, the minting, the new word, the act of inventing, the sovereign right, the quantity issued, the counterfeit, and the marketed name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一枚被冲压的坯饼走到一个被造出的词：硬币体系、铸造、新词、造词行为、君主权、发行量、赝品，以及营销名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wedge coming down on a blank disc, pressing a face into metal that had none.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块楔形模具落在空白圆片上，把一张脸压进原本没有脸的金属。

branches.en: STOCK AND ISSUE: the whole set of coins in use, then one batch struck in one year.
branches.cn: 存量与发行：流通中的整套硬币，再是某一年铸造的一批。

branches.en: WORK AND RIGHT: the labour of striking, and the sovereign permission that makes it legal.
branches.cn: 劳作与权利：冲压的劳动，以及使它合法的君主许可。

branches.en: STRUCK WORDS: a new term, and the act of inventing it.
branches.cn: 被冲压的词：新术语，以及造出它的行为。

branches.en: THE COUNTERFEIT: a stamp with nothing behind it, in metal or in language.
branches.cn: 赝品：有印记而背后无物，金属如此，语言亦如此。

branches.en: THE NAME THAT TRAVELS: a coined label built so that strangers will repeat it in a market.
branches.cn: 会走动的名字：为让陌生人在市场上反复念出来而造的品牌名。

intro.en: Coinage is a Latin-derived noun for a die plus a French suffix for process and product, and the family it belongs to still speaks of both metal and words.
intro.cn: coinage 是一个源自拉丁、指模具的名词加一个法语后缀构成，后者表过程与产物；它所属的词族至今同时谈论金属与词语。

latinIntro.en: Latin cuneus 'wedge' gives coin and coinage through French coin; Latin moneta, the mint, gives money and monetary by a separate line. The two are often confused because both concern coins.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cuneus「楔子」经法语 coin 给出 coin 与 coinage；拉丁 moneta（造币厂）经另一条线给出 money 与 monetary。两者常被混淆，因为都与硬币有关。

items.example: The die was a wedge, and the tool named the coin.
items.exampleCN: 模具是楔形的，工具便给硬币命了名。

items.meaning: a die; a piece of money
items.example: The noun still names both ends of the process.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词仍兼指过程的两端。

items.example: The suffix builds many nouns of activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成许多表活动的名词。

items.example: The compound noun is the abstract form.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合名词是抽象形式。

items.example: The agent form serves both domains.
items.exampleCN: 这个施动形式在两个领域都可用。

items.example: The gerund keeps the process in view.
items.exampleCN: 这个动名词把过程留在视野中。

items.example: The compound refers to the object, not the system.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指物件，而非体系。

items.example: The parallel noun shows the same suffix at work.
items.exampleCN: 这个同型名词显示同一后缀的运作。

items.example: A different root gives money and monetary.
items.exampleCN: 另一词根给出 money 与 monetary。

definition_zh: 货币的；金融的；（政策上）与货币供给和利率有关的；以货币计值的
definition_en: relating to money, to the supply of money in an economy, or to values expressed in money
core_image: 一间造币厂的车间，成排的圆片在传送带上被压成一样的重量与成色
scene: 央行会议室里，几位官员盯着利率曲线，讨论是否收紧银根。Monetary policy tightened before the currency lost half its value.
sceneCN: 这里 monetary 指「与货币供给和利率相关的政策层面」（第 2 个义项：作为政策领域）；句意为在货币贬值一半之前，货币政策先收紧了。

pos.zh: 货币的；金融的；以货币计值的

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 moneta（造币厂）经古法语 moneie → 钱；货币
monetary + -ism（主义）→ 货币主义（语义偏移：从属性转到学派）
monetarism + -ist（信奉者）→ 货币主义者
moneta + -ize → 货币化；铸成货币（语义偏移：从造币转到变现）
monetize + -ation（过程）→ 货币化
古英语 mynet（硬币）→ 造币厂；铸造（同族不同线）

senses.title: Relating to money as a medium
senses.titleCN: 与作为交换媒介的货币有关
senses.definition: concerned with money as the medium of exchange, including units, coins and notes
senses.definitionCN: 涉及作为交换媒介的货币，含单位、硬币与纸币
senses.example: The two states agreed to use a common monetary unit.
senses.exampleCN: 两国同意使用共同的货币单位。
senses.why: Moneta was the mint, so the adjective first describes anything belonging to coin and currency.
senses.whyCN: Moneta 是造币厂，因此这个形容词最初描述一切属于硬币与通货之物。

senses.title: Relating to the money supply as policy
senses.titleCN: 与货币供给的政策层面有关
senses.definition: concerned with the quantity of money, interest rates and central-bank action
senses.definitionCN: 涉及货币数量、利率与中央银行行动
senses.example: Monetary policy tightened before the currency lost half its value.
senses.exampleCN: 在货币贬值一半之前，货币政策先收紧了。
senses.why: Once the state manages the mint, the adjective attaches to the decisions made there.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家管理造币厂，这个形容词就附到在那里做出的决策上。

senses.title: Expressed or valued in money
senses.definition: measured, stated or compared in money terms rather than in kind
senses.definitionCN: 以货币而非实物来衡量、表述或比较
senses.example: The loss was small in monetary terms and large in reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 以货币计算损失不大，以声誉计算损失很大。
senses.why: Anything the mint measures can be described as measured by the mint's unit.
senses.whyCN: 凡是造币厂所计量的，都可用造币厂的单位来描述。

senses.title: Of a mint, in historical use
senses.titleCN: 与造币厂有关的（历史用法）
senses.definition: historical: belonging to a mint, its officers or its operations
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法：属于造币厂、其官员或其作业的
senses.example: The monetary records of the abbey list every die and every officer.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院的铸币记录列出了每一副模具与每一名官员。
senses.why: The oldest sense is literally 'of the mint', before the word widened to money in general.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项字面上就是「造币厂的」，之后才扩展到泛指货币。

senses.title: Paid in money rather than in kind
senses.definition: consisting of money, as a payment, prize or compensation
senses.definitionCN: 由钱构成的，如付款、奖金或赔偿
senses.example: The settlement included a monetary award and an apology.
senses.exampleCN: 和解方案包括一笔金钱赔偿与一份道歉。
senses.why: A payment is a use of the mint's product, so any cash component can carry the label.
senses.whyCN: 付款是造币厂产物的使用，因此任何现金部分都可带上这个标签。

senses.title: Of a shared currency area
senses.definition: describing a group of states that share one currency and one rate-setting authority
senses.definitionCN: 描述共用一种货币与一个定息当局的一组国家
senses.example: A monetary union without a common budget is fragile.
senses.exampleCN: 没有共同预算的货币联盟是脆弱的。
senses.why: If a unit can be shared, the adjective can name the arrangement that shares it.
senses.whyCN: 若一种单位可被共用，这个形容词就能指共用它的那种安排。

senses.title: Moved by money as a motive
senses.definition: concerned with money as a reason for action rather than as a measure
senses.definitionCN: 把金钱当作行动理由，而非计量尺度
senses.example: Their objections were monetary, not scientific.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的反对出于钱，而非出于科学。
senses.why: The adjective shifts from the instrument to the motive behind using it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从工具转到使用工具背后的动机。

senses.title: Contrasted with fiscal in economics
senses.definition: in economics, marking the central-bank side of policy as distinct from taxation and spending
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，标出政策中的央行一侧，与税收和支出相对
senses.example: The textbook separates monetary from fiscal tools in one chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 这本教科书用一章把货币工具与财政工具分开。
senses.why: Two arms of policy need two labels, and the mint supplies the name for one of them.
senses.whyCN: 政策的两只手臂需要两个标签，造币厂为其中一只提供了名称。

intro.en: Monetary goes back to the title of a Roman goddess whose temple held the mint, and the word for a place became the word for money itself.
intro.cn: monetary 回到一位罗马女神的称号，她的神庙设有造币厂；一个指场所的词就此成了指货币的词。

items.en: Moneta was an epithet of Juno, in whose temple on the Capitoline Hill the Roman mint stood; moneta came to mean both the mint and the money made there.
items.cn: Moneta 是朱诺的称号，罗马造币厂就设在卡比托利欧山上的她的神庙中；moneta 由此兼指造币厂与在那里造出的钱。

items.en: Why Juno carried the name Moneta is uncertain; the common link to monere 'to warn' is a hypothesis based on the goddess's advisory role, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 朱诺为何带有 Moneta 之名，来源不确定；把它与 monere「警告」相联系的通行说法，是基于这位女神的告诫职能提出的假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Monetarius meant 'of the mint' and also 'a moneyer', the official who struck coin; the adjective in English descends from this form.
items.cn: monetarius 意为「造币厂的」，也指「铸币官」，即冲压硬币的官员；英语中的形容词由这一形式而来。

items.en: Old French moneie and Middle English money carry the substance sense, while the adjective follows the learned Latin line and keeps the -ary ending.
items.cn: 古法语 moneie 与中古英语 money 承载「钱财」这一实体义，而形容词走学术拉丁那条线，保留了 -ary 词尾。

items.en: Late and medieval Latin use monetarius for anything concerning coinage, including taxes paid in coin, which is how the adjective widens beyond the building.
items.cn: 晚期与中世纪拉丁用 monetarius 指一切与铸币有关之物，包括以硬币缴纳的税，这个形容词由此越出建筑之外。

items.en: In the twentieth century monetary becomes a technical term opposed to fiscal, naming the central bank's tools rather than the treasury's.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，monetary 成为与 fiscal 相对的技术术语，指央行的工具而非财政部的工具。

note.en: The first group shares the money root or a similar shape; the second holds adjectives from neighbouring economic domains.
note.cn: 第一组共享货币词根或外形相近；第二组是邻近经济领域的形容词。

entries.definition: The thing itself, from the same mint word by the French route; monetary is the adjective built on the Latin line.
entries.definitionCN: 指钱本身，经法语路径出自同一个造币厂词；monetary 是建于拉丁那条线的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who holds a theory about the money supply; the adjective describes the domain, the noun describes a school.
entries.definitionCN: 持某种货币供给理论的人；形容词描述领域，名词描述学派。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to convert into currency or to earn revenue from something; not merely 'to be about money'.
entries.definitionCN: 意为转为货币或从某物取得收入，并非仅仅是「与钱有关」。

entries.definition: Meaning warning or admonitory, from monere 'to warn'; it looks like monetary but shares no money sense.
entries.definitionCN: 意为告诫的，来自 monere「警告」；外形像 monetary，但完全不含货币义。

entries.definition: Relating to finance, including banks, markets and corporate accounts; monetary is narrower and centres on currency and the central bank.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及金融，含银行、市场与企业账目；monetary 更窄，以货币与央行为中心。

entries.definition: Relating to government revenue and spending; economics pairs it with monetary as the two levers of policy.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及政府收入与支出；经济学把它与 monetary 并列为政策的两根杠杆。

entries.definition: A formal word for 'relating to money', chiefly in legal writing about pecuniary loss or advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 指「与钱有关的」的正式用词，主要见于法律写作中的金钱损失或利益。

entries.definition: Relating to the economy as a whole, including production and employment; monetary covers only the currency side.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及整体经济，含生产与就业；monetary 仅涵盖货币那一面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Moneta was the mint in Juno's temple: monetary means of the mint, then of money.
normal.cn: Moneta 是朱诺神庙里的造币厂：monetary 先是「造币厂的」，再是「货币的」。

normal.en: The family runs money, monetary, monetarism, monetarist, monetize, monetization, mint.
normal.cn: 同族词有 money、monetary、monetarism、monetarist、monetize、monetization、mint。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the fields: monetary policy, monetary union, monetary value, monetary compensation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分领域：货币政策、货币联盟、货币价值、金钱赔偿。

normal.en: In economics the pair is monetary and fiscal: the central bank against the treasury.
normal.cn: 经济学中的成对术语是 monetary 与 fiscal：央行对财政部。

normal.en: The false friend monitory warns, and it comes from the verb to warn, not from the mint.
normal.cn: 假朋友 monitory 意为告诫，来自「警告」那个动词，与造币厂无关。

abstract.en: Picture rows of identical discs weighed on one scale, all judged by the same number.
abstract.cn: 想象成排同样的圆片放在一杆秤上，全由同一个数字来评判。

abstract.en: Picture a committee raising a rate and watching prices fall a month later.
abstract.cn: 想象一个委员会抬高利率，一个月后看着物价下跌。

abstract.en: Picture a settlement paid in notes, with an apology added because the notes were not enough.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔以纸币支付的和解，因为纸币不够，又添上一份道歉。

examples.en: The country entered a monetary union and lost the right to set its own rate.
examples.cn: 这个国家加入货币联盟，失去了自行定息的权利。

examples.en: In monetary terms the rescue was cheap; in human terms it was not.
examples.cn: 以金钱计算，这次救援很便宜；以人的代价计算，并不便宜。

examples.en: Monetary and fiscal policy pulled in opposite directions all year.
examples.cn: 货币政策与财政政策整年都在往相反方向拉。

dict_mnemonic.text: moneta（造币厂）+ ary（…的）＝ 造币厂那一套的；先记「一间厂」，再记「一套政策」。

root: 拉丁 moneta（朱诺称号，其神庙设造币厂，由此兼指造币厂与钱币）+ -arius（属于…的）→ 晚期拉丁 monetarius → 英语 monetary；Moneta 与 monere「警告」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start at a mint building and end at a policy label: money as medium, the money supply, value in money, the historical mint, payment in cash, a currency area, money as motive, and the economics pairing with fiscal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一间造币厂开始，落到一个政策标签：作为媒介的货币、货币供给、以钱计值、历史上的造币厂、现金支付、货币区、金钱动机，以及经济学中与财政并列的一侧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mint where every disc is weighed to the same standard, and that single number then judges everything else.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间造币厂把每枚圆片都称到同一标准，而那一个数字随后评判其余一切。

branches.en: PLACE AND MEDIUM: the building and its officers first, then the money they make as a medium of exchange.
branches.cn: 场所与媒介：先是建筑与官员，再是他们造出的作为交换媒介的钱。

branches.en: MANAGED SUPPLY: a state that runs the mint also sets the rate, and states that share a rate form a union.
branches.cn: 被管理的供给：经营造币厂的国家也定利率，共用利率的国家则组成联盟。

branches.en: MEASURE AND PAYMENT: anything can be priced in the unit, and anything can be paid in it.
branches.cn: 计量与支付：任何东西都可用这个单位标价，也都可用它支付。

branches.en: MONEY AS REASON: the instrument becomes a motive when people object on monetary grounds.
branches.cn: 钱作为理由：当人们以钱为由反对时，工具就成了动机。

branches.en: ONE OF TWO LEVERS: economics needs a name for the central-bank arm as against the treasury.
branches.cn: 两根杠杆之一：经济学需要给央行这只手臂一个与财政部相对的名称。

intro.en: Monetary is a Latin adjective of the mint, and the root behind it also gives the plain English noun for money and the vocabulary of monetary theory.
intro.cn: monetary 是一个指造币厂的拉丁形容词，其词根还给出英语中指钱的普通名词与货币理论的整套词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin moneta 'mint, money' gives money through French and monetary, monetize and monetarism through the learned line. The related verb monere 'to warn' gives monitory, which is a different word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 moneta「造币厂、钱」经法语给出 money，经学术线给出 monetary、monetize 与 monetarism。相关动词 monere「警告」给出 monitory，那是另一个词。

items.example: The root names the place before it names the money.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根先指场所，再指钱。

items.structure: monetarius (Latin adjective and noun, 'of the mint; moneyer')
items.example: The Latin adjective supplies the English form.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词提供英语形式。

items.example: The suffix marks relation rather than substance.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出关系，而非实体。

items.example: The adjective is the learned member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是家族中的学术成员。

items.example: The plain noun came by the French route.
items.exampleCN: 这个普通名词是经法语路径来的。

items.example: The verb extends the mint to any source of revenue.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把造币厂扩展到任何收入来源。

items.meaning: a theory of the money supply
items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a school.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成学派。

items.example: The person form follows the doctrine form.
items.exampleCN: 人称形式跟在学说形式之后。

items.example: The look-alike comes from the verb to warn, not from the mint.
items.exampleCN: 这个形近词来自「警告」那个动词，与造币厂无关。

definition_zh: 征税；税制；税收；（比喻）沉重的负担；（法律）费用核定
definition_en: the system by which a government raises money through taxes, or the money so raised
core_image: 征税窗口前排着长队，每张单据都被盖上一个红章，钱从一只手转到另一只手
scene: 税务局的窗口前，店主把一叠票据递进去，计算器按得飞快。Taxation of small shops rose while the larger firms received credits.
sceneCN: 这里 taxation 指「政府对小商户征税这一制度性行为」（第 1 个义项：作为整套税制）；句意为小店铺的税负上升，而较大的企业拿到抵免。

pos.zh: 征税；税制；税收（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 taxare（核定、估值）→ 税；征税
tax + -able（可…的）→ 应纳税的
tax + payer（支付者）→ 纳税人
tax + -ing → 费力的（语义偏移：从征税转到耗损）
over-（过度）+ tax → 课税过重；使负担过重
sur-（在上、附加）+ tax → 附加税；加征附加税

senses.title: The system of raising money by taxes
senses.titleCN: 以税收筹集资金的制度
senses.definition: the organized system by which a government imposes and collects taxes
senses.definitionCN: 政府课征并收取税款的有组织制度
senses.example: Taxation of small shops rose while the larger firms received credits.
senses.exampleCN: 小店铺的税负上升，而较大的企业拿到抵免。
senses.why: Taxare meant to assess a value, and -ation names the process, so the word is the assessing done systematically.
senses.whyCN: taxare 意为核定价值，-ation 指过程，因此这个词就是被系统化执行的核定。

senses.title: The act of imposing a tax
senses.definition: the single act or occasion of placing a tax on a person, good or activity
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某货品或某活动设定税负的单次行为
senses.example: The taxation of the new service began in April.
senses.exampleCN: 对这项新服务征税从四月开始。
senses.why: The process noun can denote one instance, as with many nouns of action.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词可指单次事例，许多表动作的名词都是如此。

senses.title: The money raised as taxes
senses.definition: the revenue collected through taxes, considered as a sum
senses.definitionCN: 经税收收取的财政收入，作为一笔总额来看
senses.example: Taxation paid for the road, though drivers complained about it.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路是用税款修的，尽管司机们仍有怨言。
senses.why: The result of assessing is the assessed sum, so the process noun also carries the product.
senses.whyCN: 核定的结果就是被核定的款额，因此过程名词也承载产物。

senses.title: The burden borne by a group
senses.definition: the weight of taxes on a particular class of people or on a sector
senses.definitionCN: 某一类人或某个部门所承担的税负之重
senses.example: The report measures the taxation of the poorest tenth.
senses.exampleCN: 报告衡量最贫困的十分之一人口所承受的税负。
senses.why: A system is felt as weight, and the same word shifts from institution to experience.
senses.whyCN: 制度被感受为重量，同一个词便从机构转到体验。

senses.title: Assessing the value of property
senses.definition: historical and legal: the official valuation of property or income as the basis for a charge
senses.definitionCN: 历史与法律用法：作为收费依据对财产或所得的官方估值
senses.example: The taxation of the estate took three months of surveying.
senses.exampleCN: 对这份地产的估值用了三个月勘测。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is to touch and assess, so valuation survives inside the modern tax word.
senses.whyCN: 词根最古老的义项是触碰与估值，因此估值之义留在现代的税词里。

senses.title: A heavy demand on patience or strength
senses.titleCN: 对耐心或体力的沉重消耗
senses.definition: figuratively, a severe strain placed on a person's endurance or goodwill
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指对某人耐力或善意的严重消耗
senses.example: Three hours of questioning was a taxation of his patience.
senses.exampleCN: 三个小时的盘问是对他耐心的一次消耗。
senses.why: Anything that assesses and takes a share can describe what people are asked to give up.
senses.whyCN: 任何核定并抽取一份的东西，都能描述人被迫让出的部分。

senses.title: The settling of costs in court
senses.definition: legal: the official fixing and allowance of costs in a case, as a taxation of costs
senses.definitionCN: 法律用法：对案件费用所作的官方核定与准许，如「费用核定」
senses.example: The taxation of costs was left to the registrar.
senses.exampleCN: 费用核定交由书记官办理。
senses.why: Court costs are assessed line by line, and English law kept the older word for assessment.
senses.whyCN: 诉讼费用逐项核定，英国法保留了「核定」这一较老的说法。

senses.title: The revenue side of fiscal policy
senses.titleCN: 财政政策中的收入一侧
senses.definition: in public finance, the revenue-raising half of policy, paired with public spending
senses.definitionCN: 在公共财政中，与公共支出并列的筹资一半
senses.example: The budget balances taxation against expenditure.
senses.exampleCN: 预算在税收与支出之间求平衡。
senses.why: A system of collection becomes one half of a policy pair, and the word stands for that half.
senses.whyCN: 征收体系成为一对政策中的一半，这个词就代表那一半。

intro.en: Taxation is the process noun built on a Latin verb for assessing value, and the assessing sense is still visible inside it.
intro.cn: taxation 是建于一个表核定价值的拉丁动词之上的过程名词，核定义仍能在其中看见。

items.en: Taxare meant 'to assess, to value, to impose a charge'. It is usually taken as a frequentative of tangere 'to touch, to handle'.
items.cn: taxare 意为「核定、估值、课以费用」。它通常被视为 tangere「触碰、处理」的反复形式。

items.en: Tangere 'to touch' supplies the physical image behind assessment: a value is handled and found to be so much. The link to taxare is generally accepted but reconstructed.
items.cn: tangere「触碰」提供核定背后的实体形象：价值被摸过一遍，定出多少。它与 taxare 的联系一般被接受，但属重构。

items.en: Medieval Latin taxa meant a rate or a charge, and taxa and taxare together gave the European words for a tax.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 taxa 指税率或费用，taxa 与 taxare 一并给出欧洲诸语言中表税的诸词。

items.en: Old French taxer 'to impose a tax' is the form English borrowed, first as a verb in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 taxer「课税」是英语借入的形式，十三世纪先以动词出现。

items.en: English tax appears as noun and verb in the fourteenth century; taxation follows as the noun of action, using the Latin -ation ending rather than a native one.
items.cn: 英语 tax 在十四世纪以名词与动词出现；taxation 随后作为动作名词出现，用的是拉丁 -ation 词尾而非本族词尾。

items.en: English law keeps taxation for the assessing of costs, and public finance uses it for the revenue side of the budget, so one word serves a courtroom and a treasury.
items.cn: 英国法保留 taxation 指费用核定，公共财政用它指预算的收入一侧，同一个词同时服务法庭与国库。

note.en: The first group is formed on the same stem and is easily confused; the second holds words for particular charges and for the act of imposing them.
note.cn: 第一组建于同一词干，容易混淆；第二组是具体税费与课征行为的说法。

entries.definition: One charge, or the act of imposing it; taxation is the system, the process or the revenue as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一项税，或课征它的动作；taxation 是制度、过程或整体税收。

entries.definition: As an adjective it means demanding or exhausting; it is not a noun for the tax system.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词时意为费力、耗人的；它不是指税制的名词。

entries.definition: Meaning subject to tax, said of income, goods or persons; it marks liability, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 指应纳税的，用于收入、货品或人；它标出责任，而非制度。

entries.definition: The person or firm that pays; the word names a party where taxation names a system.
entries.definitionCN: 付税的个人或企业；taxation 指制度，这个词指一方当事人。

entries.definition: A charge imposed by authority, often one-off; taxation is the standing system rather than a single raising.
entries.definitionCN: 由当局课征的收费，常为一次性；taxation 是常设制度，而非单次征收。

entries.definition: A tax on particular goods, especially imports; it is one kind of tax within a taxation system.
entries.definitionCN: 对特定货物、尤指进口货所征的税；是税制中的一类。

entries.definition: A schedule of duties on imports, or the duty itself; it is narrower than the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 进口关税表，或指该关税本身；比整个税制窄。

entries.definition: The act of fixing a value or a charge, which is the literal core of taxation but without the revenue frame.
entries.definitionCN: 确定价值或收费的行为；这是 taxation 的字面核心，但不带财政收入框架。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: tax 'assess' + -ation 'process': the assessing of everyone, done every year.
normal.cn: tax「核定」+ -ation「过程」：对所有人做的核定，年年做一遍。

normal.en: The family runs tax, taxation, taxable, taxpayer, taxing, overtax, tax-free.
normal.cn: 同族词有 tax、taxation、taxable、taxpayer、taxing、overtax、tax-free。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the system: double taxation, progressive taxation, taxation without representation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出制度：双重征税、累进税制、无代表不纳税。

normal.en: The courtroom keeps the old sense: a taxation of costs is an assessment, not a tax.
normal.cn: 法庭保留了旧义：费用核定是估值，不是税。

normal.en: The word buys roads and courts, so the burden sense and the revenue sense are the same coin.
normal.cn: 这个词买来道路与法庭，因此「负担」义与「收入」义是同一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a queue at a window where every slip receives the same red stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象窗口前的长队，每张单据都盖上同一个红章。

abstract.en: Picture a road built by many small payments nobody remembers making.
abstract.cn: 想象一条由许多无人记得付过的小额款项修成的路。

abstract.en: Picture an hour of questioning that takes more out of a person than any bill.
abstract.cn: 想象一小时的盘问，从人身上取走的东西比任何账单都多。

examples.en: Progressive taxation takes a larger share from higher incomes.
examples.cn: 累进税制从较高收入中取走更大的份额。

examples.en: The colony objected to taxation without representation.
examples.cn: 这块殖民地反对无代表而纳税。

examples.en: The taxation of costs added more than the damages themselves.
examples.cn: 费用核定加上去的钱比赔偿金本身还多。

dict_mnemonic.text: tax（核定、征税）+ ation（过程）＝ 挨个核定收钱这件事；记住窗口、红章与长队。

root: 拉丁 taxare「核定、估值、课以费用」（一般为 tangere「触碰、处理」的反复形式）→ 中世纪拉丁 taxa「税率」→ 古法语 taxer → 英语 tax + -ation → taxation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow money from a valuation to a policy half: the system, one imposition, the revenue, the felt burden, the older valuation, the strain on patience, the court's cost assessment, and the revenue side of the budget.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让钱从一次估值走到政策的一半：制度、一次课征、税款、被感受到的负担、较早的估值、对耐心的消耗、法庭的费用核定，以及预算的收入一侧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a value is handled, a share is fixed, and the share is taken out of someone's hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份价值被摸过，一份份额被定下，而这份份额从某人手里被取走。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND SINGLE ACT: the standing machinery, then one switch of that machinery turned on.
branches.cn: 制度与单次行为：常设的机器，再是这台机器被打开一次。

branches.en: MONEY IN AND MONEY OUT: what is collected becomes the revenue half of a budget.
branches.cn: 收进来与花出去：收得的钱成为预算的收入一半。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: a system is known by how it feels on the tenth of the population that pays most of its income.
branches.cn: 重量：一套制度如何，看它对缴纳收入最大份额的那十分之一人口是什么感受。

branches.en: THE OLD ASSESSMENT: valuation of property and of court costs keeps the root sense alive outside the treasury.
branches.cn: 古老的核定：对财产与诉讼费用的估值让词根本义在国库之外存活。

branches.en: THE SAME WORD FOR EFFORT: anything that takes a share can take it out of patience instead of pocket.
branches.cn: 同一个词也指消耗：任何抽取份额者，可以从口袋里抽，也可以从耐心里抽。

intro.en: Taxation is the Latin process noun of a Latin verb of assessment, and English still uses the bare verb and a small family of adjectives around it.
intro.cn: taxation 是一个拉丁核定动词的拉丁过程名词，英语至今仍使用那个光秃秃的动词以及围绕它的少量形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin taxare 'to assess' gives tax, taxation, taxable and overtax; the older tangere 'to touch' is generally seen as its base. The same root family supplies taximeter and therefore taxi, by the charge sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 taxare「核定」给出 tax、taxation、taxable 与 overtax；更古老的 tangere「触碰」一般被视为其基础。同一词根家族经「收费」义给出 taximeter，并由此给出 taxi。

items.structure: taxare (Latin verb, first conjugation, 'to assess, charge')
items.example: The verb is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的基础。

items.example: Assessment began as handling a thing to value it.
items.exampleCN: 核定起初是摸过一件东西以估其价值。

items.structure: tax (English noun and verb from taxare)
items.example: The bare form works as noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个光秃形式兼作名词与动词。

items.example: The suffix forms the abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成抽象名词。

items.example: The process noun is the formal term.
items.exampleCN: 这个过程名词是正式术语。

items.example: The suffix marks liability, not activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出责任，而非活动。

items.example: The compound names the party on the other side.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指另一侧的当事人。

items.example: The participle moved from charging to draining.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词从「课征」偏移到「耗损」。

items.example: The prefix measures excess rather than kind.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀衡量的是过度，而非种类。

definition_zh: 税；税款；征税；使负担沉重；（旧）指责；（旧）核定价值
definition_en: a compulsory payment to a government on income, goods or property, or the act of imposing one
core_image: 柜台上一张单据被划上红笔，一栏写着应缴，一栏写着已缴
scene: 报税季的桌面上摊满单据，会计师逐项核对可以抵扣的支出。A new tax on sugar changed what the factory put in its bottles.
sceneCN: 这里 tax 指「对某种货品征收的一项税」（第 2 个义项：作为具体的税种）；句意为新开征的糖税改变了工厂往瓶子里放的东西。

pos.zh: 税；税款（可数或不可数）
征税；使负担沉重；（旧）指摘；核定价值

derivatives.zh: tax + -ation（过程）→ 征税；税制
tax + -able（可…的）→ 应纳税的
tax + payer → 纳税人
tax + -ing → 费力的；耗人的（语义偏移：从课征转到消耗）
tax + free（免除）→ 免税的
sur-（在上）+ tax → 附加税

senses.title: A compulsory payment to government
senses.titleCN: 向政府强制缴纳的款项
senses.definition: a payment required by law, levied on income, goods, property or activity, and used for public purposes
senses.definitionCN: 由法律规定、对所得、货品、财产或活动课征并用于公共用途的款项
senses.example: Income tax is withheld before the salary reaches the account.
senses.exampleCN: 所得税在工资到账之前就被扣下。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to assess a value, and a compulsory payment is a value officially assessed and taken.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为核定价值，而强制缴纳的款项正是被官方核定并取走的价值。

senses.title: A particular charge on something
senses.titleCN: 对某物征收的具体税种
senses.definition: one named duty on a specified good or activity, such as a sugar tax or a fuel tax
senses.definitionCN: 对特定货品或活动具名课征的一项税，如糖税、燃油税
senses.example: A new tax on sugar changed what the factory put in its bottles.
senses.exampleCN: 新开征的糖税改变了工厂往瓶子里放的东西。
senses.why: A system is made of items, and each item takes the same countable noun.
senses.whyCN: 制度由项目组成，而每一项目都用这个可数名词。

senses.title: Taxes as a collective burden
senses.definition: the total weight of taxation on a person, a firm or a class
senses.definitionCN: 落在某个人、某企业或某一阶层身上的全部税负
senses.example: The poorest pay a larger share of their income in tax.
senses.exampleCN: 最贫困者要从收入中拿出更大比例来缴税。
senses.why: Many separate charges are felt as one weight, and the plural or mass use carries that feeling.
senses.whyCN: 许多单独的费用被感受为一份重量，复数或不可数用法正承载这种感受。

senses.title: To impose a charge on someone
senses.definition: to levy a tax on a person, good or activity by authority
senses.definitionCN: 由当局对某人、某货品或某活动课征税款
senses.example: The city taxes every vehicle that enters the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市对每辆进入老城的车辆征税。
senses.why: The verb is the official act behind the noun: assess, fix a rate, and require payment.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词背后的官方行为：核定、定率、要求缴纳。

senses.title: To strain or test someone
senses.titleCN: 使某人吃力或受考验（比喻）
senses.definition: figuratively, to put a heavy demand on patience, strength or a resource
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指对耐心、体力或某种资源提出沉重的要求
senses.example: The last mile taxed the runners more than the first ten.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一英里比前十英里更让跑者吃力。
senses.why: A tax takes a share, and effort takes a share of strength; the metaphor is the same subtraction.
senses.whyCN: 税取走一份，effort 也从体力里取走一份；这个比喻是同一个减法。

senses.title: To accuse someone of something
senses.definition: archaic: to charge or accuse a person with a fault, as to tax someone with carelessness
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法：指摘某人的过失，如责备某人粗心
senses.example: The old letters tax him with neglect of his estate.
senses.exampleCN: 那些旧书信指摘他荒废了自己的产业。
senses.why: To charge a person with a fault and to charge a person with a sum use the same verb of imposing.
senses.whyCN: 以过失加之于人，与以款额加之于人，用的是同一个「施加」动词。

senses.title: To assess the value of property
senses.definition: historical: to value property or goods officially as a basis for a charge
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法：为收费依据而对财产或货物作官方估值
senses.example: The sheriff taxed the land before the levy was set.
senses.exampleCN: 郡守在定税之前先对土地估值。
senses.why: This is the root sense unclouded: to touch a thing and say what it is worth.
senses.whyCN: 这是未被遮蔽的词根本义：摸过一件东西，说出它值多少。

senses.title: A demand on a shared resource
senses.definition: a charge on a natural or public resource, treated as a cost of using it
senses.definitionCN: 对自然或公共资源所课的费用，被视为使用它的代价
senses.example: A tax on water changed how the farms irrigated.
senses.exampleCN: 对水课征的费用改变了农场的灌溉方式。
senses.why: If a charge can guide behaviour, it can be put on a resource as easily as on income.
senses.whyCN: 若收费能引导行为，那么它能落在资源上，与落在收入上同样容易。

senses.title: A burden written into a price
senses.definition: the portion of a price that consists of tax, often passed to the buyer
senses.definitionCN: 价格中由税构成的那一部分，常转嫁给买方
senses.example: The ticket's tax is printed separately at the bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 票价里的税在底部单独印出。
senses.why: A charge that can be passed along becomes a line in a price, and the word follows it there.
senses.whyCN: 可以转嫁的费用成了价格里的一行，这个词也就跟到那里。

intro.en: Tax is the bare verb-noun pair from which taxation is built, and its oldest sense is not collection but valuation by touch.
intro.cn: tax 是构成 taxation 的那对光秃的动词与名词，其最古老的义项不是收取，而是以触碰来估值。

items.en: Taxare meant 'to assess, value, impose a charge'. It is generally taken as a frequentative of tangere, marking repeated handling.
items.cn: taxare 意为「核定、估值、课以费用」。它一般被视为 tangere 的反复形式，标出反复的处理。

items.en: Tangere 'to touch, handle' supplies the physical image: a thing is handled, and its worth is fixed. The derivation is generally accepted but reconstructed.
items.cn: tangere「触碰、处理」提供实体形象：一件东西被处理过，其价值被定下。该派生一般被接受，但属重构。

items.en: Medieval Latin taxa named a rate or a fixed charge, and taxa and taxare together spread the tax words across Europe.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 taxa 指税率或固定费用，taxa 与 taxare 一并把「税」这个词散布到欧洲各地。

items.en: English takes the verb taxer from Old French in the thirteenth century, at first for imposing a charge and for accusing.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪从古法语接来动词 taxer，起初既指课征费用，也指指摘。

items.en: The noun tax follows in the fourteenth century, and the accusing sense survives in legal and literary writing long after the money sense dominates.
items.cn: 名词 tax 在十四世纪跟上；指摘义在金钱义占据主导之后很久，仍留在法律与文学写作中。

items.en: From the sixteenth century to tax someone or something means to strain it, since a levy takes a share of whatever it falls on.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，to tax someone or something 意为使其吃力，因为课征总要从所落之处取走一份。

note.en: The first group is formed on the same short stem; the second holds particular charges and the verbs of imposing them.
note.cn: 第一组建于同一个短词干；第二组是具体税费与课征它们的动词。

entries.definition: The abstract process noun for the whole system; tax is the single charge or the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指整套制度的抽象过程名词；tax 是单项税或那个动作。

entries.definition: Meaning exhausting or demanding, which is sense five of the verb turned into an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 意为耗人的、费力的，是动词第五个义项转成的形容词。

entries.definition: Subject to tax; it describes a status rather than an amount or a system.
entries.definitionCN: 应纳税的；它描述一种地位，而非款额或制度。

entries.definition: Shortened from taximeter, the fare meter, whose root is the same charge word; it is related by the sense of charging, not by meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 由 taximeter（计费表）缩略而来，其词根正是同一个「收费」词；两者由收费义相连，而非由词义相连。

entries.definition: A charge imposed, or the act of raising one, often used for one-off or wartime charges.
entries.definitionCN: 所课征的费用，或征收行为，常用于一次性或战时的课征。

entries.definition: A tax on particular goods, especially imports; it is one species of tax.
entries.definitionCN: 对特定货物、尤指进口货所征的税；是 tax 的一个种类。

entries.definition: A list of duties on imports, or one such duty; it is narrower and trade-specific.
entries.definitionCN: 进口关税表，或其中一项关税；更窄且专用于贸易。

entries.definition: A charge for using a road, bridge or tunnel; it buys passage rather than funding a government.
entries.definitionCN: 使用道路、桥梁或隧道的费用；它买的是通行，而非供养政府。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means to touch and value a thing: first you assess it, then you take a share.
normal.cn: 词根意为摸过并估值：先核定，再取走一份。

normal.en: The family runs tax, taxation, taxable, taxpayer, taxing, tax-free, surtax, overtax.
normal.cn: 同族词有 tax、taxation、taxable、taxpayer、taxing、tax-free、surtax、overtax。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the kind: income tax, a tax on imports, tax avoidance, tax evasion.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类别：所得税、进口税、避税、逃税。

normal.en: The metaphor is subtractive: a long climb taxes the legs as a levy taxes the purse.
normal.cn: 这个比喻是减法：长坡消耗双腿，如课税消耗钱包。

normal.en: The old accusing sense survives in writing: to tax someone with a fault.
normal.cn: 旧的指摘义留在书面语中：指摘某人的过失。

abstract.en: Picture a slip of paper with two columns, one for what is owed and one for what is paid.
abstract.cn: 想象一张两栏的单据，一栏写应缴，一栏写已缴。

abstract.en: Picture a shop changing its recipe because a charge was put on one ingredient.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店因为某种原料被课费而改了配方。

abstract.en: Picture a runner whose last mile costs more than the first ten put together.
abstract.cn: 想象一位跑者，最后一英里的代价超过前十英里之和。

examples.en: The government raised the tax on tobacco and lowered it on books.
examples.cn: 政府提高烟草税，降低书籍税。

examples.en: Every household pays a fixed tax for waste collection.
examples.cn: 每户都为垃圾清运缴纳固定费用。

examples.en: Reading three drafts in one afternoon taxed her eyes more than her patience.
examples.cn: 一下午读三份草稿，耗损她的眼力甚于耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: tax＝先摸一遍估值，再从中取走一份；记「一张两栏的单据」，一栏应缴、一栏已缴。

root: 拉丁 taxare「核定、估值、课以费用」，一般为 tangere「触碰、处理」的反复形式；中世纪拉丁 taxa「税率」→ 古法语 taxer → 英语 tax。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one subtraction in view: a compulsory payment, one named charge, the total burden, the act of imposing, the strain on a person, the old accusation, the old valuation, a charge on a resource, and a tax buried in a price.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项守住同一个减法：强制缴纳、某个具名税种、全部负担、课征的动作、对人的消耗、旧的指摘、旧的估值、对资源的收费，以及埋在价格里的税。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a value is handled, a share is marked on a slip, and the share leaves the pocket.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份价值被处理，一份份额被标在单据上，然后这份份额离开口袋。

branches.en: ITEM AND TOTAL: one compulsory payment, then all of them felt together as a weight.
branches.cn: 单项与总额：一笔强制缴纳，再把全部合并感受为一份重量。

branches.en: NAMED AND HIDDEN: a sugar tax with a name, and a tax already folded into a ticket price.
branches.cn: 具名与隐藏：有名有姓的糖税，与已经折进票价里的税。

branches.en: IMPOSING ON THINGS: the official act, and the same act applied to water rather than income.
branches.cn: 对物课征：官方行为本身，以及同一行为落在水上而非收入上。

branches.en: THE SAME SUBTRACTION: what a levy takes from a purse, effort takes from a body.
branches.cn: 同一个减法：课征从钱包里取走的，effort 从身体里取走。

branches.en: THE OLD VERB: charging a person with a fault and valuing a piece of land are the same gesture of laying something on someone or something.
branches.cn: 古老的动词：以过失加之于人与为一块地估值，都是把某物加到某人或某物上的同一手势。

intro.en: Tax is a short borrowed stem that takes native and Latin endings alike, and its small family covers collection, liability and exhaustion.
intro.cn: tax 是一个短小的借来词干，本族与拉丁词尾都能接，其小词族涵盖征收、责任与耗损。

latinIntro.en: Latin taxare 'to assess' is the base, with tangere 'to touch' generally seen behind it; the endings -ation, -able and the compound payer are English additions. The fare meter behind taxi descends from the same charging sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 taxare「核定」是基础，一般被视为其后的 tangere「触碰」；-ation、-able 与复合成分 payer 都是英语添加的。taxi 背后的计费表也出自同一个收费义。

items.example: The Latin verb is the source of the stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是词干的来源。

items.example: The stem is shorter than its Latin original.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干比其拉丁原形短。

items.example: Only taxation carries this ending.
items.exampleCN: 只有 taxation 带这个词尾。

items.example: Taxable marks what may be charged.
items.exampleCN: taxable 标出可被课征之物。

items.example: The compound personifies the charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把费用人格化。

items.example: Taxing moved from levying to exhausting.
items.exampleCN: taxing 从课征偏移到耗损。

items.example: The compound removes the charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词取消了费用。

items.example: The prefix stacks one charge on another.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把一层费用叠在另一层上。

items.example: The prefix measures excess.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀衡量过度。
